depth-012.p: Which goddess sprang fully armed from Zeus's head, according to myth?
depth-012.e: Athena is correct. She is associated with wisdom and strategic warfare.

depth-014.p: On which mountain did the Olympian gods live?
depth-014.e: Olympus is correct. It is also the highest mountain in Greece.

depth-015.p: Which creature had a lion's head, a goat's head on its back and a snake for a tail?
depth-015.e: The Chimera is correct. Bellerophon defeated it with help from Pegasus.

depth-016.p: Which creature asked a riddle at the entrance to Thebes?
depth-016.e: The Sphinx is correct. Oedipus solved the riddle about the ages of man.

depth-017.p: Which three-headed dog guarded the underworld?
depth-017.e: Cerberus is correct. Heracles brought it back as his last labour.

depth-018.p: In the original Greek myth, Pandora's box was not a box at all. What was it?
depth-018.e: In Hesiod, Pandora opens a large clay jar, a pithos. Only in the 1500s was the word translated as box, and that version stuck.

depth-019.p: Which conflict, according to the myth, was triggered by a dispute over a golden apple?

o.o2: The war between the Titans and the gods
o.o3: The war between the Lapiths and the Centaurs
o.o4: The campaign of the Seven against Thebes

depth-019.e: Paris gave the apple marked for the fairest to Aphrodite. Her promise of Helen became the start of the conflict that led to the Trojan War.

depth-021.p: Which god is associated with poetry and eloquence?
depth-021.e: Bragi is correct. He is described as the poet of the gods.

depth-023.p: Who is the god of the sea, wind and wealth?
depth-023.e: Njord is correct. He is the father of Freyr and Freyja.

depth-024.p: Which god owns the ship Skidbladnir?
depth-024.e: Freyr is correct. The ship can be folded together and always gets a fair wind.

depth-028.p: Which animal gnaws at one of the roots of Yggdrasil?
depth-028.e: The dragon Nidhogg is correct. It lives near the spring Hvergelmir.

depth-029.p: What does Ratatoskr do in the stories about the world tree Yggdrasil?

o.o1: Carries insults between the eagle and the dragon

depth-029.e: The squirrel Ratatoskr runs up and down Yggdrasil with mocking messages between the eagle in the crown and Nidhogg at the root.

depth-030.p: What is the name of the world of humans in Norse mythology?
depth-030.e: Midgard is correct. It lies between the worlds of the gods and the giants.

depth-032.p: Which hall receives warriors chosen by Odin?
depth-032.e: Valhalla is correct. The valkyries lead the chosen there.

depth-033.p: What is the name of Odin's spear, which never misses its target?
depth-033.e: Gungnir is correct. The dwarves, the sons of Ivaldi, forged the spear.

depth-034.p: What is the name of the magical fetter around Fenrir?
depth-034.e: Gleipnir is correct. It looks thin, but is stronger than iron.

depth-035.p: What is the name of the ring that drips eight new rings every ninth night?
depth-035.e: Draupnir is correct. Odin placed the ring on Baldur's funeral pyre.

depth-037.p: What happens to the sun at Ragnarok?

o.o3: Surt puts it out with his sword

depth-037.e: The wolf Skoll swallowing it is correct. Skoll has chased the sun across the sky.

depth-040.p: How many worlds are normally connected by Yggdrasil?
depth-040.e: Nine is correct. The nine worlds include Asgard, Midgard and Jotunheim, among others.

depth-041.p: How many roots does the Prose Edda describe Yggdrasil as having?
depth-041.e: Three is correct. The roots stretch towards different worlds and wells.

depth-043.e: Sirius Black is correct. He was James Potter's close friend and a member of the Order of the Phoenix.

depth-045.p: Who is the head of the Hufflepuff house?
depth-045.e: Pomona Sprout is correct. She also teaches herbology.

depth-049.p: What is the name of the wizarding village near Hogwarts?
depth-049.e: Hogsmeade is correct. Students from third year can visit the village with permission.

depth-052.p: Where does the Weasley family live?
depth-052.e: The Burrow is correct. The crooked house lies near the village of Ottery St Catchpole.

depth-054.p: Which object sorts new students into Hogwarts' houses?
depth-054.e: The Sorting Hat is correct. The hat takes the pupil's qualities and wishes into account.

depth-055.p: What is a Time-Turner used for?

o.o2: Seeing a day into the future

depth-055.e: Travelling back a few hours is correct. Hermione uses one in her third school year.

depth-056.p: What does Dumbledore keep in a Pensieve?
depth-056.e: Memories is correct. The memories can be viewed from outside as living scenes.

depth-057.p: Which creature pulls the carriages to Hogwarts for those who can see it?
depth-057.e: Thestrals is correct. They can only be seen by people who have witnessed and understood a death.

depth-058.e: A phoenix is correct. Fawkes' tears have healing powers.

depth-059.p: Which creature lives in the school's secret chamber?
depth-059.e: A basilisk is correct. Its direct gaze is deadly.

depth-060.p: What kind of creature is Dobby?
depth-060.e: A house-elf is correct. He becomes free when he receives a sock.

depth-061.p: Which spell makes light come from the wand?
depth-061.e: Lumos is correct. The counter-spell that puts out the light is Nox.

depth-062.p: Which spell is used to repair a broken object?
depth-062.e: Reparo is correct. Hermione uses the magic on Harry's glasses, among other things.

depth-063.e: Accio is correct. The object flies towards the person who casts the spell.

depth-065.p: Which subject does Professor Binns teach?
depth-065.e: History of Magic is correct. Binns continued teaching as a ghost.

matrix-cat-22-music-front-3.p: Who is the lead singer of Volbeat?
matrix-cat-22-music-front-3.e: Michael Poulsen is correct. The band blends heavy rock with inspiration from 1950s rockabilly.

matrix-cat-22-music-front-4.p: Who is the lead singer of The Minds of 99?
matrix-cat-22-music-front-4.e: Niels Brandt is correct. The band is known for its Danish-language songs and large concert productions.

matrix-cat-22-music-front-6.p: Who is the lead singer of D-A-D?
matrix-cat-22-music-front-6.e: Jesper Binzer is correct. The name was shortened from Disneyland After Dark after a legal objection.

matrix-cat-43-bake-technique-2.p: How are the many thin layers in a croissant created?

o.o1: The dough is folded around layers of cold butter
o.o2: The dough is whipped airy before the flour is added
o.o3: The butter is mixed into the dough
o.o4: The dough is briefly boiled before baking

matrix-cat-43-bake-technique-2.e: Lamination folds dough and cold butter into many layers. During baking the water turns to steam, which lifts the layers apart.

matrix-cat-44-drink-serve-6.p: How is a classic Dry Martini served after stirring?

o.o1: Strained into a chilled cocktail glass without ice
o.o2: In a tall glass filled with crushed ice
o.o3: In a short glass over a large ice cube
o.o4: Unstrained in a warm cocktail glass

matrix-cat-44-drink-serve-6.e: A Dry Martini is stirred with ice and usually strained into a chilled cocktail glass. The ice is used for chilling and dilution, but does not go into the glass.

format-depth-001.p: Which technology came first on the market?
format-depth-001.e: Betamax came out in 1975, a year before VHS. The CD followed in 1982 and the MiniDisc in 1992.

format-depth-002.e: Wikipedia launched in 2001; the others followed in 2004, 2005 and 2006.

format-depth-004.e: Sputnik 1 entered orbit in 1957; Yuri Gagarin flew in 1961.

o.o4: The first video shared on YouTube

format-depth-005.e: Ray Tomlinson sent networked email in 1971; the handheld mobile call followed in 1973.

format-depth-006.e: Frankenstein was published in 1818, before the other three classics.

format-depth-007.p: Which sporting event took place first?

o.o4: The first Formula One World Championship

format-depth-007.e: The first modern Olympics were held in Athens in 1896.

format-depth-008.p: Which Danish cultural event came first?

o.o3: The Fall of the King named book of the century

format-depth-008.e: Matador began in 1978; the other events came later.

format-depth-009.e: Alexander Graham Bell's telephone patent dates from 1876, before Edison's phonograph from 1877.

format-depth-010.p: Which one doesn't belong among these moons?
format-depth-010.e: Mars is a planet; Europa, Titan and Triton are moons.

format-depth-012.p: Which one doesn't belong among these Nordic capitals?
format-depth-012.e: Tallinn is the capital of Estonia and therefore Baltic, not Nordic.

format-depth-013.p: Which one doesn't belong among these instruments?
format-depth-013.e: The clarinet is a woodwind instrument; the others are string instruments.

format-depth-014.p: Which one doesn't belong among these painting movements?
format-depth-014.e: Bauhaus was a design and architecture school; the others are mainly art movements.

format-depth-015.p: Which one doesn't belong among these blood vessels?
format-depth-015.e: The trachea carries air, while the other three carry blood.

format-depth-017.p: Which one doesn't belong among these EU institutions?
format-depth-017.e: NATO is a defence alliance, not an EU institution.

format-depth-018.p: Which one doesn't belong among these baking techniques?
format-depth-018.e: Sautéing means cooking over high heat; the others are often used in baking and confectionery.

format-depth-021.p: Which one doesn't belong among these Greek gods?

format-depth-022.p: Which one doesn't belong among these philosophical movements?
format-depth-022.e: Baroque is a cultural and historical style period, not a philosophical school.

format-depth-026.p: True or false: A year on Mercury is shorter than a day measured from sunrise to sunrise.
format-depth-026.e: Mercury takes 88 Earth days to orbit the Sun, while a solar day lasts 176 Earth days.

format-depth-027.p: True or false: All mammals give birth to live young.
format-depth-027.e: The platypus and the echidna are mammals, but they lay eggs.

format-depth-028.p: True or false: Glass at room temperature is a very slowly flowing liquid.
format-depth-028.e: Ordinary glass is an amorphous solid; the thickness of old window panes is due to how they were made.

format-depth-029.p: True or false: Lightning can strike the same place several times.
format-depth-029.e: Tall buildings such as skyscrapers are often struck repeatedly.

format-depth-031.p: True or false: The Great Wall of China can clearly be seen from the Moon with the naked eye.
format-depth-031.e: The wall is too narrow and has too little contrast with its surroundings.

format-depth-032.p: True or false: Denmark has had negative interest rates on some government bonds.
format-depth-032.e: Investors have at times accepted a small cost to hold Danish bonds for their safety.

format-depth-033.p: True or false: A red card in football can be given to a substitute on the bench.
format-depth-033.e: The rules on discipline apply to substitutes as well as to players who have been substituted.

format-depth-034.p: True or false: A browser and a search engine are the same thing.
format-depth-034.e: The browser displays web pages; a search engine is a service you use through the browser.

format-depth-035.p: True or false: Sourdough can raise bread without added baker's yeast.
format-depth-035.e: Sourdough contains natural yeasts and lactic acid bacteria.

format-depth-037.p: Which food can stay edible for a very long time if stored dry and sealed?
format-depth-037.e: Honey's low water content and acidity inhibit microorganisms.

format-depth-038.p: Which planet rotates almost on its side?
format-depth-038.e: Uranus's axis of rotation tilts about 98 degrees.

format-depth-040.p: Which organ can regrow a large part of its mass after an operation?
format-depth-040.e: The liver can grow back to a functional size, even though its shape changes.

format-depth-041.p: What colour is a polar bear's skin under its fur?
format-depth-041.e: The dark skin can absorb solar energy, while the hairs are mostly transparent.

format-depth-042.p: Which metal can melt in a warm hand?
format-depth-042.e: Gallium melts at around 30 degrees, but it should not be used as a toy.

format-depth-045.p: Which bird can fly backwards in controlled flight?
format-depth-045.e: The hummingbird's wing movement can create lift in both directions.

format-depth-047.p: Which body part analyses the scent particles a snake collects with its tongue?

o.o1: Jacobson's organ in the roof of the mouth
o.o2: Taste buds along the tip of the tongue
o.o3: Olfactory cells in the snake's lungs
o.o4: A sense organ behind the eardrum

format-depth-047.e: The tongue collects chemical particles and delivers them to Jacobson's organ in the roof of the mouth, also called the vomeronasal organ.

o.o2: Image of a black hole's shadow

format-depth-050.e: Gravitational waves were measured in 2015; the other milestones came in 2019, 2022 and 2023.

format-depth-052.p: Which one doesn't belong among these learning concepts?
format-depth-052.e: Osmosis is the transport of water through a membrane, not a learning theory.

format-depth-056.p: What function does the central executive have in Baddeley's model of working memory?
format-depth-056.e: The central executive coordinates, among other things, phonological and visuospatial processing.

format-depth-057.p: What characterises secure attachment in Ainsworth's Strange Situation?

o.o1: The child seeks comfort and settles down

format-depth-057.e: The adult acts as a secure base to which the child can return.

format-depth-060.p: What does the Gestalt principle of closure describe?

o.o1: The brain fills in missing parts
o.o2: Things close together are seen as a group
o.o3: The same shape is seen as a group
o.o4: A figure is seen apart from its background

format-depth-060.e: We tend to perceive incomplete outlines as whole shapes.

format-depth-061.p: Which three needs are central to self-determination theory?
format-depth-061.e: The theory links the three psychological needs to intrinsic motivation and well-being.

format-depth-066.p: Which animal can survive frozen during the winter months?
format-depth-066.e: The wood frog tolerates much of its body fluid freezing, while sugars protect its cells.

format-depth-070.p: What characterises a predominantly internal locus of control?

o.o1: Outcomes stem from one's own choices and actions
o.o2: Outcomes are due to luck and chance

format-depth-070.e: Internal locus of control means that a person relatively strongly experiences their own actions as significant for what happens.

format-depth-071.e: A harmless signal often attracts less attention when it is repeated many times.

format-depth-072.p: Which Danish TV series follows families around the radio and TV industry after 1945?
format-depth-072.e: The Chronicles follows four main characters through Denmark's transformation from 1949 to 1973.

wikithin-danish-film-director-Q352000.p: Who directed the film Adam's Apples?
wikithin-danish-film-director-Q352000.e: Anders Thomas Jensen directed the film Adam's Apples.

wikithin-danish-film-director-Q110365.p: Who directed the film Dancer in the Dark?
wikithin-danish-film-director-Q110365.e: Lars von Trier directed the film Dancer in the Dark.

wikithin-danish-film-director-Q196103.p: Who directed the film Love Is All You Need?
wikithin-danish-film-director-Q196103.e: Susanne Bier directed the film Love Is All You Need.

wikithin-danish-film-director-Q1327845.p: Who directed the film After the Wedding?
wikithin-danish-film-director-Q1327845.e: Susanne Bier directed the film After the Wedding.

wikithin-danish-film-director-Q775356.p: Who directed the film The Idiots?
wikithin-danish-film-director-Q775356.e: Lars von Trier directed the film The Idiots.

wikithin-danish-film-director-Q1326419.p: Who directed the film King's Game?
wikithin-danish-film-director-Q1326419.e: Nikolaj Arcel directed the film King's Game.

wikithin-danish-film-director-Q370707.p: Who directed the film Pelle the Conqueror?
wikithin-danish-film-director-Q370707.e: Bille August directed the film Pelle the Conqueror.

wikithin-danish-film-director-Q316761.e: Nicolas Winding Refn directed the film Pusher.

wikithin-danish-film-director-Q312394.p: Who directed the film The House of the Spirits?
wikithin-danish-film-director-Q312394.e: Bille August directed the film The House of the Spirits.

wikithin-danish-literature-author-Q11924.p: Who wrote The Concept of Anxiety?
wikithin-danish-literature-author-Q11924.e: Søren Kierkegaard wrote the work The Concept of Anxiety.

wikithin-danish-literature-author-Q17562.e: Karen Blixen wrote the work Out of Africa.

wikithin-danish-literature-author-Q76718.p: Who wrote Miss Smilla's Feeling for Snow?
wikithin-danish-literature-author-Q76718.e: Peter Høeg wrote the work Miss Smilla's Feeling for Snow.

wikithin-danish-literature-author-Q21807.p: Who wrote Jeppe of the Hill?
wikithin-danish-literature-author-Q21807.e: Ludvig Holberg wrote the work Jeppe of the Hill.

wikithin-danish-literature-author-Q16426.e: Martin Andersen Nexø wrote the work Pelle the Conqueror.

wikithin-danish-literature-author-Q17578.e: Steen Steensen Blicher wrote the work Præsten i Vejlbye.
Karen Blixen wrote the work Seven Gothic Tales.

wikithin-danish-series-creator-Q1211796.p: Who created the TV series The Bridge?
wikithin-danish-series-creator-Q1211796.e: Hans Rosenfeldt created the TV series The Bridge.

wikithin-danish-series-creator-Q956446.p: Who created the TV series The Killing?
wikithin-danish-series-creator-Q956446.e: Søren Sveistrup created the TV series The Killing.

wikithin-danish-series-creator-Q1331994.p: Who created the TV series The Kingdom?
wikithin-danish-series-creator-Q1331994.e: Lars von Trier created the TV series The Kingdom.

wikithin-danish-series-creator-Q12333582.p: Who created the TV series Rita?
wikithin-danish-series-creator-Q12333582.e: Christian Torpe created the TV series Rita.

wikithin-invention-inventor-Q2270.e: Michael Faraday discovered the substance benzene.

wikithin-invention-inventor-Q143.e: Ludwik Lejzer Zamenhof created the language Esperanto.

wikithin-invention-inventor-Q43484.p: Which philosopher wrote about the Übermensch in Thus Spoke Zarathustra?
wikithin-invention-inventor-Q43484.e: Friedrich Nietzsche is associated with the concept of the Übermensch.

wikithin-invention-inventor-Q10693.e: Dmitri Mendeleev devised the periodic table.

wikithin-invention-inventor-Q2294.p: Who is considered the discoverer of the proton?
wikithin-invention-inventor-Q2294.e: Ernest Rutherford is associated with the discovery of the proton.

wikithin-invention-inventor-Q144334.p: Who developed movable metal type printing in Europe?
wikithin-invention-inventor-Q144334.e: Johann Gutenberg is associated with the development of the European printing press.

variety-001.p: Rank the planets from closest to furthest from the Sun.
variety-001.e: The first four planets from the Sun are Mercury, Venus, Earth and Mars.

variety-002.p: Put the Danish monarchs in order of their accession to the throne.
variety-002.e: Christian IV came to the throne in 1588, Frederick VII in 1848, Christian X in 1912 and Margrethe II in 1972.

variety-003.p: Rank the inventions from oldest to newest.
variety-003.e: The printing press came around 1450, the telephone in 1876, the radio in the 1890s and the World Wide Web in 1989.

variety-004.p: Put the works in order of their first publication.
variety-004.e: Hamlet dates from around 1600, Pride and Prejudice from 1813, On the Origin of Species from 1859 and 1984 from 1949.

variety-005.p: Rank the sporting events by when they were first held.
variety-005.e: The modern Olympics began in 1896, the Tour de France in 1903, the football World Cup in 1930 and the Formula One World Championship in 1950.

variety-006.p: Put the audio formats in order from oldest to newest.
variety-006.e: The phonograph came in 1877, magnetic tape in the 1920s, the compact cassette in 1963 and the CD commercially in 1982.

variety-007.p: Rank the bridges by opening year.

variety-008.p: Rank these technologies by breakthrough, oldest first.
variety-008.e: The steam engine came long before the transistor in 1947, the microprocessor in 1971 and the modern smartphone in the 2000s.

variety-009.p: Roughly how many square kilometres is Denmark's land area?
variety-009.e: Denmark's land area is about 42,952 km², excluding Greenland and the Faroe Islands.

variety-010.p: Roughly how many kilometres is it on average from Earth to the Moon?
variety-010.e: The Moon's average distance from Earth is around 384,400 kilometres.

variety-011.p: How many bones does a normal adult human have?
variety-011.e: An adult human skeleton is normally considered to consist of 206 bones.

variety-012.p: Roughly how high is Denmark's highest natural point, Møllehøj?
variety-012.e: Møllehøj measures about 170.86 metres above sea level.

variety-013.p: Roughly how fast does sound travel in dry air at 20 °C?
variety-013.e: The speed of sound in dry air at 20 °C is roughly 343 metres per second.

variety-014.p: How many numbered symphonies are traditionally attributed to Mozart?
variety-014.e: Mozart's traditional symphony catalogue ends at Symphony No. 41, the Jupiter Symphony.

variety-015.p: How many Olympian gods are traditionally counted?
variety-015.e: The classical group is called the Twelve Olympians, although its membership can vary.

variety-016.p: How many elements does the periodic table officially have?
variety-016.e: IUPAC recognises 118 elements, from hydrogen to oganesson.

o.o1: The fall of the Berlin Wall

variety-017.e: The Macintosh was launched in 1984, before Live Aid in 1985, Chernobyl in 1986 and the fall of the Berlin Wall in 1989.

o.o2: Nelson Mandela became president of South Africa
o.o4: Dolly the sheep was cloned in Scotland

variety-018.e: Nelson Mandela became president in 1994; Windows 95, Dolly and Google followed later.

variety-019.e: Wikipedia was launched in 2001, YouTube in 2005, the iPhone in 2007 and Spotify in 2008.

variety-020.p: Which event came first in the 2010s?
variety-020.e: Instagram was launched in 2010, before the Paris Agreement, the Brexit referendum and Disney+.

variety-021.e: The Sopranos premiered in 1999, before The Wire, Mad Men and Breaking Bad.

variety-022.e: Doom came out in 1993, The Sims in 2000, World of Warcraft in 2004 and the first version of Minecraft in 2009.

variety-023.p: Which Danish music release came out first?

o.o2: No Fuel Left for the Pilgrims by D-A-D
o.o4: Efter endnu en dag by Gasolin'

variety-023.e: Gasolin's Efter endnu en dag came out in 1976, before the D-A-D, Aqua and Agnes Obel albums.

variety-024.p: Which football tournament was founded first?
variety-024.e: The FA Cup was founded in 1871 and is older than the other competitions.

variety-025.p: Which of these animals is not a mammal?
variety-025.e: The tuna is a fish; dolphins, bats and seals are mammals.

variety-027.p: Which one doesn't belong among creatures from Norse mythology?
variety-027.e: Pegasus is the winged horse from Greek mythology.

variety-028.p: Which one doesn't belong as a microphone type?
variety-028.e: A compressor is a signal processor, not a microphone type.

variety-029.p: Which one doesn't belong among the planets?
variety-029.e: Europa is one of Jupiter's moons, not a planet.

variety-030.p: Which one doesn't belong as a programming language?
variety-030.e: HTML is a markup language; the others are used as programming languages.

variety-033.p: True or false: Sound can travel through a vacuum.
variety-033.e: Sound requires a medium such as air, water or solid matter, so it cannot travel through a vacuum.

variety-034.p: True or false: A day on Venus is longer than a year on Venus.
variety-034.e: Venus rotates so slowly that its sidereal day is longer than its orbit around the Sun.

variety-035.p: True or false: Gutenberg invented printing before Columbus reached America.
variety-035.e: Gutenberg's printing technique spread around 1450; Columbus reached the Caribbean in 1492.

variety-036.p: True or false: Polar bears naturally live in both the Arctic and the Antarctic.
variety-036.e: Polar bears live in the Arctic; the Antarctic has penguins but no wild polar bears.

variety-037.p: True or false: Karen Blixen also published books under the name Isak Dinesen.
variety-037.e: Isak Dinesen was Karen Blixen's best-known English-language pen name.

variety-038.p: True or false: The Roskilde Festival was first held in 1972.
variety-038.e: The first festival was held in 1971 under the name Sound Festival.

variety-039.p: True or false: The Danish Constitution was signed on 4 June 1849.
variety-039.e: Frederick VII signed the June Constitution on 5 June 1849.

variety-040.p: True or false: A goalkeeper may pick up a deliberate back-pass from a teammate's foot with their hands.
variety-040.e: The back-pass rule forbids the goalkeeper from picking up, with the hands, a deliberate pass played with the foot.

variety-042.p: Who wrote the short line “To be or not to be”?
variety-042.e: The words open Hamlet's famous soliloquy in Shakespeare's tragedy Hamlet.

variety-043.p: Who wrote “To travel is to live”?
variety-043.e: The phrase is associated with H.C. Andersen's autobiographical work The Fairy Tale of My Life.

variety-044.p: Which Danish politician is associated with the words “One has a position until one takes a new one”?
variety-044.e: Jens Otto Krag used the phrasing in connection with changed political positions.

variety-045.p: Who is described? He has one hand, lost as a pledge when Fenrir was bound.
variety-045.e: Tyr placed his hand in the wolf's jaws as a guarantee and lost it when the wolf discovered the deceit.

variety-047.p: Which animal is described? It is the largest living animal in the world and feeds on small crustaceans.
variety-047.e: The blue whale can grow over 25 metres long and filters mainly krill from the water.

variety-050.p: Which statement about atoms is incorrect?

o.o1: Protons have a negative electric charge

variety-050.e: Protons have a positive charge; it is electrons that have a negative charge.

variety-053.p: Music meets geography: Which city is associated with the grunge movement around Nirvana?
variety-053.e: Seattle became the centre of the grunge scene, with Nirvana, Pearl Jam and Soundgarden among others.

variety-054.p: History meets technology: Which war is associated with the famous codebreaking of the Enigma machine?
variety-054.e: Allied codebreakers worked during the Second World War to read German Enigma traffic.

variety-057.p: Which motorsport event has Tom Kristensen won nine times?
variety-057.e: Tom Kristensen's nine wins in the 24-hour race at Le Mans earned him the nickname Mr. Le Mans.

variety-060.p: Which country is especially known for brunost?
variety-060.e: Norwegian brunost gets its colour and sweetness from boiling down and caramelising whey.

variety-061.p: Which Finnish dish is described? Fish and pork are baked inside a dense rye loaf.
variety-061.e: Kalakukko is a traditional Finnish dish from Savonia, where the filling is cooked inside rye bread.

variety-064.p: True or false: Members of the European Parliament are elected directly by citizens.
variety-064.e: Direct elections to the European Parliament have been held since 1979.

variety-067.p: Who is associated with classical conditioning and experiments on dogs' salivary reflex?
variety-067.e: Pavlov showed how a neutral stimulus can trigger a learned response through association.

variety-068.p: Who developed attachment theory, focusing on children's close caregiving relationships?
variety-068.e: John Bowlby described attachment as a biologically rooted system that seeks closeness and security.

variety-071.p: How many disciplines does a decathlon consist of?
variety-071.e: The decathlon combines ten athletics events spread over two competition days.

variety-073.p: Which sport is described? The players hit a shuttlecock over a net.
variety-073.e: Badminton is played with rackets and a shuttlecock, which is markedly slowed down by the air.

variety-075.p: Where in the Nordic region do musk oxen live wild in larger numbers?
variety-075.e: Greenland has large populations of musk oxen, although some populations have been moved between areas.

variety-076.p: Which North Atlantic bird is described? It has a colourful beak and breeds in colonies on cliffs.
variety-076.e: The puffin is also called a sea parrot and uses its colourful beak to carry several small fish.

variety-077.p: True or false: Reindeer naturally occur only south of the Arctic Circle.
variety-077.e: Reindeer are adapted to tundra and northern forest areas in both Eurasia and North America.

variety-082.p: Which process is described? Yeast converts sugar into alcohol and carbon dioxide.
variety-082.e: In alcoholic fermentation, yeast breaks down sugar and forms ethanol and carbon dioxide, among other things.

variety-084.p: In what year did the Chernobyl disaster take place?
variety-084.e: The reactor accident at Chernobyl took place on 26 April 1986.

variety-086.p: In what year was the Hubble Space Telescope launched?
variety-086.e: Hubble was sent into orbit by the space shuttle Discovery in April 1990.

variety-087.p: Which film from 1995 was the first fully computer-animated feature film?
variety-087.e: Pixar's Toy Story from 1995 was the first feature film made entirely with computer animation.

variety-088.p: Which game series began in Japan in 1996 with collectable monsters?
variety-088.e: The first Pokémon games were released for the Game Boy in Japan in 1996.

variety-089.p: Which electronics brand launched the portable cassette player the Walkman?
variety-089.e: Sony launched the first Walkman in 1979 and made the name synonymous with portable music.

variety-090.p: Which sportswear brand is especially associated with three parallel stripes?
variety-090.e: Adidas has used the three stripes as a central trademark since the company's early years.

variety-091.p: Which car brand uses the model names Corolla, Prius and Yaris?
variety-091.e: Corolla, Prius and Yaris are three different model lines from Toyota.

variety-092.p: What does albedo describe in climate research?

o.o1: How much light a surface reflects

variety-092.e: Albedo is the share of incoming sunlight that a surface reflects; white snow therefore has a high albedo.

variety-093.p: Which process makes the sea more acidic when it absorbs more carbon dioxide?
variety-093.e: Dissolved carbon dioxide reacts with water to form carbonic acid, which lowers the pH of seawater.

variety-094.p: What are the pieces in Tetris called, each made up of four squares?
variety-094.e: Tetris pieces are tetrominoes: shapes made of exactly four equal-sized squares.

variety-096.p: Which material is used for the frame of a Nether portal in Minecraft?
variety-096.e: A Nether portal is built from obsidian and is normally activated with flint and steel.

variety-097.p: Which genre does the Civilization series primarily belong to?
variety-097.e: Civilization is a turn-based strategy series in which a civilisation develops through historical eras.

variety-098.p: Which studio developed the original Pokémon Red and Green?
variety-098.e: Game Freak developed the first Pokémon games, which Nintendo published for the Game Boy in Japan.

variety-101.p: Which researcher developed the Strange Situation test of young children's attachment?
variety-101.e: Mary Ainsworth used the Strange Situation to study different attachment patterns.

variety-103.p: What is RAM mainly used for in a computer?
variety-103.e: RAM provides quick, temporary access to the data and programs the computer is working with right now.

variety-107.p: What does it mean to blind-bake a pie crust?

o.o1: To bake the base before the filling is added
o.o2: To bake without turning on the oven light
o.o3: To cover the pie completely with dough

variety-107.e: Blind-baking pre-bakes the base, often with baking paper and weights, so that it does not go soggy under the filling.

variety-108.p: Which gas makes yeast dough rise?
variety-108.e: Yeast converts sugar and forms carbon dioxide, among other things, which is trapped in the dough's gluten network.

variety-112.p: What is a dishwasher's special salt mainly intended for?
variety-112.e: The salt regenerates the machine's ion exchanger, which softens the water and limits limescale deposits.

variety-119.p: Which Norwegian dish is traditionally made from dried fish treated with lye?
variety-119.e: Lutefisk is made from dried whitefish that is soaked and treated with lye before cooking.

theme-60-001.p: Where must the One Ring be destroyed?
theme-60-001.e: The Ring can only be destroyed in the fire where Sauron forged it.

theme-60-002.p: What is the name of the hobbit who carries the Ring from the Shire?
theme-60-002.e: Frodo takes over the Ring from Bilbo and sets out for Mordor.

theme-60-003.p: What was Gollum called before the Ring transformed him?
theme-60-003.e: Sméagol finds the Ring after Déagol's discovery and is slowly consumed by it.

theme-60-004.p: What name does Aragorn's sword receive when it is reforged?
theme-60-004.e: Andúril is forged from the shards of Narsil and becomes a sign of Aragorn's heritage.

theme-60-005.p: Who is the oldest Ent the hobbits meet in Fangorn?
theme-60-005.e: Treebeard leads the Ents' council and their march against Isengard.

theme-60-006.p: Which land do the Rohirrim defend?
theme-60-006.e: Rohan is known for its horsemen and is ruled from Meduseld in Edoras.

theme-60-007.p: Which city is the capital of Gondor during the War of the Ring?
theme-60-007.e: Minas Tirith is the fortified city besieged by Sauron's armies.

theme-60-008.e: Lembas keeps for a long time and gives a great deal of nourishment on a journey.

theme-60-009.p: What creature do the dwarves awaken deep beneath Moria?
theme-60-009.e: The balrog is a fire spirit from the First Age, later called Durin's Bane.

theme-60-010.p: In which town is the inn The Prancing Pony located?
theme-60-010.e: In Bree the hobbits meet Aragorn, who goes there under the name Strider.

theme-60-011.p: Which creature does Shelob most resemble?
theme-60-011.e: Shelob guards a tunnel on the border of Mordor.

theme-60-012.p: Which people does Legolas belong to?
theme-60-012.e: Legolas is a Wood-elf and the son of King Thranduil.

theme-60-013.e: Glóin was himself part of Bilbo's journey to the Lonely Mountain.

theme-60-014.p: What did Sam Gamgee work as at home in the Shire?
theme-60-014.e: Sam tends the garden at Bag End, among other things, before the journey begins.

theme-60-016.p: Who defeats the Witch-king on the Pelennor Fields?
theme-60-016.e: Éowyn fights alongside Merry and strikes down the leader of the Nazgûl.

theme-60-017.p: How many members does the Fellowship have when it leaves Rivendell?
theme-60-017.e: The nine members symbolically face the nine Ringwraiths.

theme-60-018.p: Which gift from Galadriel helps Frodo in Shelob's lair?
theme-60-018.e: The phial holds light from Eärendil's star and frightens Shelob.

theme-60-019.e: The two young hobbits become part of the Fellowship of the Ring.

theme-60-020.p: Which creature does Gandalf ride after his return?
theme-60-020.e: Shadowfax is the fastest of Rohan's horses and accepts Gandalf as his rider.

theme-60-021.p: Who wrote the novel The Lord of the Rings?
theme-60-021.e: Tolkien published the work in three volumes from 1954 to 1955.

theme-60-022.p: Which book tells of Bilbo's journey and the finding of the Ring?
theme-60-022.e: The Hobbit recounts, among other things, how Bilbo finds the Ring.

theme-60-023.p: Who had the Ring immediately before Bilbo?
theme-60-023.e: Bilbo finds the Ring in Gollum's cave beneath the Misty Mountains.

theme-60-024.e: They were men-kings who became enslaved by their Rings of power and by Sauron.

theme-60-026.p: Which symbol is most clearly associated with Sauron's surveillance?
theme-60-026.e: The Eye of Sauron symbolises his search for the Ring and his far-reaching power.

theme-60-028.p: What came first in the story of Middle-earth?
theme-60-028.e: Bilbo finds the Ring decades before Frodo's journey begins.

theme-60-029.p: Which statement about the One Ring is correct?

o.o1: It prolongs the life of a mortal bearer
o.o3: It can only be carried by hobbits
o.o4: It loses its power outside Mordor

theme-60-029.e: The Ring stretches life, but at the same time it wears down its bearer.

theme-60-030.p: Who gathers an army of Uruk-hai at Isengard?
theme-60-030.e: Saruman builds his military strength in Isengard and sends the Uruk-hai against Rohan.

theme-60-031.e: Orthanc is the black tower at the centre of Isengard, where Saruman dwells.

theme-60-032.p: Who often refers to the Ring as 'my precious'?
theme-60-032.e: Gollum's speech shows how strongly the Ring has bound his identity to itself.

theme-61-001.p: On which planet does Luke Skywalker grow up?
theme-61-001.e: Luke grows up with his aunt and uncle on a moisture farm on Tatooine.

theme-61-002.p: Which planet is Princess Leia's home world?
theme-61-002.e: Alderaan is destroyed by the Death Star in the first film.

theme-61-004.p: Which species does Chewbacca belong to?
theme-61-004.e: Wookiees come from the forest planet Kashyyyk.

theme-61-006.p: Who was the main target of Order 66?
theme-61-006.e: The clones were ordered to turn against their Jedi generals.

theme-61-007.p: What type of droid is C-3PO?
theme-61-007.e: C-3PO is built for etiquette, translation and communication between species.

theme-61-008.p: What is R2-D2 especially built for?
theme-61-008.e: As an astromech droid, R2-D2 helps pilots and starships, among other things.

theme-61-009.p: Who was Obi-Wan Kenobi's Jedi master?
theme-61-009.e: Qui-Gon trains Obi-Wan and finds Anakin on Tatooine.

theme-61-010.p: What characterises Darth Maul's first lightsaber?

o.o2: It can be split into three

theme-61-010.e: The red, staff-shaped lightsaber is revealed in the duel on Naboo.

theme-61-012.p: Who provides the genetic template for the clone army?
theme-61-012.e: The clones are created from Jango Fett's DNA on Kamino.

theme-61-014.p: What is Kylo Ren's birth name?
theme-61-014.e: Ben is the son of Leia Organa and Han Solo.

theme-61-015.p: On which planet does Rey live as a scavenger?
theme-61-015.e: Rey waits for her family among the wrecks from an old space battle.

theme-61-016.e: The name Finn is formed from the letters in FN-2187.

theme-61-017.p: Which large battle machines attack the rebel base on Hoth?
theme-61-017.e: The four-legged AT-AT machines attack the shield generator at Echo Base.

theme-61-018.p: Which people help the rebels on the forest moon of Endor?
theme-61-018.e: The Ewoks use the terrain and simple traps against the Empire's forces.

theme-61-019.p: What does a parsec actually measure?
theme-61-019.e: A parsec is an astronomical unit of length, although the word is used in a famous line about the Kessel Run.

theme-61-020.p: Who was Ahsoka Tano's Jedi teacher?
theme-61-020.e: Ahsoka becomes Anakin's padawan during the Clone Wars.

theme-61-021.p: What is the group in Rogue One trying to steal?
theme-61-021.e: The stolen plans reveal the design flaw that the rebels later exploit.

theme-61-023.p: Which crystal traditionally powers a lightsaber?
theme-61-023.e: The kyber crystal focuses the weapon's energy and is associated with the Force.

theme-61-024.e: Jabba is a powerful Hutt gangster based on Tatooine.

theme-61-025.p: Which city does Lando Calrissian administer?
theme-61-025.e: Cloud City floats in Bespin's atmosphere and mines tibanna gas.

theme-61-026.e: X-wing starfighters are used, among other things, in the attack on the Death Star.

theme-61-027.p: What does the Sith rule of two mean?

o.o2: A Sith may only live for two decades
o.o3: There is one master and one apprentice

theme-61-027.e: The rule is meant to limit internal strife and concentrate dark power in two Sith.

theme-61-029.p: What came first in Anakin's life?

o.o3: He fights in the Clone Wars

theme-61-029.e: The podrace on Tatooine takes place before Anakin is admitted to the Jedi Order.

theme-61-030.p: Why is Star Wars Day celebrated on 4 May?

o.o1: The first film premiered that day
o.o2: George Lucas was born that day
o.o3: The Death Star was destroyed that day
o.o4: The date sounds like the pun 'May the Force'

theme-61-030.e: 'May the Fourth' sounds in English like the beginning of the series' famous greeting.

theme-61-036.p: What colour are the rebel pilots' classic flight suits?
theme-61-036.e: The orange suit is seen, among other places, on X-wing pilots in the original trilogy.

theme-62-001.p: In which short film did Mickey Mouse have his big breakthrough in 1928?
theme-62-001.e: Steamboat Willie became famous for its synchronised sound.

theme-62-003.p: Who is Simba's father in The Lion King?
theme-62-003.e: Mufasa is king of the Pride Lands before Scar takes over the throne.

theme-62-004.p: What is the name of the kingdom in Frozen?
theme-62-004.e: Anna and Elsa are princesses in the fictional Nordic kingdom of Arendal.

theme-62-005.p: What is the family called in Encanto?
theme-62-005.e: The Madrigal family's magical house gives almost all the children a special gift.

theme-62-006.p: Which ability does Moana learn to rediscover?
theme-62-006.e: She continues her people's tradition as a wayfinder, using the stars and the sea.

theme-62-007.p: Why does Mulan join the army?

o.o1: She is looking for her brother
o.o4: She wants to win the emperor's crown

theme-62-007.e: Mulan disguises herself to spare her ageing father from military service.

theme-62-008.p: What is the name of the city where Aladdin meets Jasmine?
theme-62-008.e: Agrabah is the fictional city where the palace and the market are.

theme-62-009.p: Which object shows the time of the Beast's curse?
theme-62-009.e: The curse must be broken before the last rose petal falls.

theme-62-012.p: Who wants to make a fur coat from the dalmatian puppies?
theme-62-012.e: Cruella is the villain in 101 Dalmatians and is obsessed with fur.

theme-62-014.p: Who is Hercules' father in the Disney film?
theme-62-014.e: Hercules is born the son of Zeus and Hera, but loses most of his divinity.

theme-62-015.p: Who raises Tarzan as a baby?
theme-62-015.e: Kala takes Tarzan in after his parents die.

theme-62-016.p: What is the name of the cowboy doll in Toy Story?
theme-62-016.e: Woody is Andy's favourite toy before Buzz Lightyear arrives.

theme-62-017.p: What kind of fish is Nemo?
theme-62-017.e: Nemo and his father Marlin are clownfish, while Dory is a surgeonfish.

theme-62-018.p: What is the surname of the superhero family in The Incredibles?
theme-62-018.e: Bob, Helen, Violet, Dash and Jack-Jack are all named Parr.

theme-62-019.p: What is the name of the rat who dreams of becoming a chef?
theme-62-019.e: Rémy controls Linguini's movements and helps him in the restaurant kitchen.

theme-62-021.p: Which holiday forms the setting of Coco?
theme-62-021.e: Miguel travels to the land of the dead during the Mexican Día de Muertos.

theme-62-022.p: What animal is Judy Hopps in Zootopia?
theme-62-022.e: Judy becomes Zootopia's first rabbit police officer.

theme-62-023.e: Stitch is created as Experiment 626 by the scientist Jumba.

theme-62-024.p: What is special about Rapunzel's hair in Tangled?
theme-62-024.e: The power of her hair comes from a magical sunflower.

o.o4: The South Seas island of Motunui

theme-62-025.e: On Neverland children never grow up, and Peter leads the Lost Boys.

theme-62-026.p: What kind of animal is Bambi?
theme-62-026.e: Bambi is a little fawn who grows up in the forest.

theme-62-027.p: How many dwarfs does Snow White live with?
theme-62-027.e: The seven dwarfs each have their own name and personality traits.

theme-62-028.p: What is WALL-E built to do?
theme-62-028.e: The robot tidies up an abandoned Earth by compacting rubbish.

decade-quality-050.e: OLED does not need the same backlight as a classic LCD panel and can switch off individual pixels completely.

decade-quality-051.p: What makes USB-C practical compared with older USB-A?

o.o3: It can be inserted either way round

decade-quality-051.e: USB-C describes the shape of the connector; the supported speeds and power can vary between cables and devices.

decade-quality-055.p: In which Danish crime series is Sarah Lund the central investigator?
decade-quality-055.e: Sarah Lund, played by Sofie Gråbøl, became internationally known together with the series' distinctive knitted jumper.

decade-quality-056.p: Which two urban areas were linked more closely when the Øresund Bridge opened in 2000?
decade-quality-056.e: The Øresund link consists of a bridge, an artificial island and a tunnel between the capital region and Skåne.

decade-quality-057.p: What was Snapchat's original distinctive feature?

o.o2: Messages of no more than 140 characters

decade-quality-057.e: Snapchat launched in 2011 and made temporary image messages its central idea.

decade-quality-059.p: Which country voted in 2016 to leave the EU?
decade-quality-059.e: A majority of 51.9 per cent voted to leave the EU; the withdrawal took effect in 2020.

decade-quality-060.p: What is RCS developed as a modern successor to or extension of?
decade-quality-060.e: RCS can support group chat, read receipts and higher-quality images than classic SMS, among other features.

decade-quality-062.p: Why is a one-time code useful for two-step verification?

o.o1: The code makes the account anonymous
o.o2: A stolen password alone is not enough
o.o4: It hides the user's email address

decade-quality-062.e: A time-limited code or an approval on another device adds an extra proof of the user's identity.

decade-quality-063.p: Why can dark mode save power on some OLED screens?

o.o3: The screen turns the internet off

decade-quality-063.e: On OLED each pixel emits its own light. On LCD screens the backlight is normally on regardless of the pixel colour.

decade-quality-064.p: Which country hosted the Summer Olympics in 2016?
decade-quality-064.e: The Games were held in Rio de Janeiro and were the first Olympic Games in South America.

decade-quality-065.p: What does the measure CO₂e express?

o.o1: The combined effect of greenhouse gases
o.o4: The oxygen level in air samples

decade-quality-065.e: CO₂-equivalents convert different greenhouse gases by their warming effect so they can be compared.

philosophy-quality-001.p: What do the so-called Gettier cases show?

o.o1: Justified true belief is not always knowledge
o.o3: The senses are always better than logic

philosophy-quality-001.e: Gettier cases describe situations in which a person has a justified and true belief, but only hits the truth by chance. They challenge a classical definition of knowledge.

philosophy-quality-002.p: What does the Stoics’ distinction between control and non-control come down to?

o.o1: Focusing on our own choices, not the rest

philosophy-quality-002.e: The Stoics distinguished between our own judgements and actions and the external circumstances we cannot master. Calm is found by directing our efforts towards the first.

philosophy-quality-003.p: What is the core of David Hume’s problem of ‘is’ and ‘ought’?

o.o1: Ought cannot be derived from facts alone
o.o2: The majority makes facts morally right
o.o3: Rules only apply if consequences are measured
o.o4: Descriptions of nature are always value-laden

philosophy-quality-003.e: Hume drew attention to the leap from statements about how the world is to statements about how it ought to be. At least one normative premise is required.

philosophy-quality-004.p: Why did Karl Popper emphasise falsifiability in science?

o.o1: A theory must be capable of being refuted
o.o2: A theory must be conclusively provable
o.o4: Theories must be based on known measurements

philosophy-quality-004.e: For Popper a scientific theory is risky: one must be able to describe an observation that would contradict it. Confirmations alone are not enough.

philosophy-quality-005.p: What is Robert Nozick’s thought experiment about an experience machine meant to investigate?

o.o1: Whether pleasure alone makes life good
o.o2: Whether a machine can choose more fairly
o.o3: Whether memories are real outside the brain

philosophy-quality-005.e: Nozick asked us to imagine a machine that provides perfect experiences. Many people would not want to be connected, suggesting that we also value reality, action and identity.

philosophy-quality-006.p: What does Sartre’s formulation “existence precedes essence” mean?
philosophy-quality-006.e: For Sartre, human beings have no predetermined nature or purpose. We first exist and then shape ourselves through our choices.

philosophy-quality-007.p: How does Albert Camus describe the absurd?

o.o1: The search for meaning meets a silent world

philosophy-quality-007.e: For Camus the absurd arises from the tension between our need for meaning and a world that gives no clear answer. He recommends revolt and presence rather than resignation.

philosophy-quality-009.p: What did Epicurus especially associate with a good and pleasant life?

o.o1: Absence of pain and mental disturbance
o.o2: The greatest possible pleasure every day

philosophy-quality-009.e: Epicurus recommended moderation, friendship and peace of mind. Pleasure did not mean constant abundance, but above all freedom from pain and unnecessary fear.

philosophy-quality-010.p: What characterises the Socratic method of conversation?
philosophy-quality-010.e: Socrates is associated with an investigative questioning technique, in which unclear concepts and hidden contradictions are brought to light through conversation.

music-quality-reggae-offbeat-001.p: What often creates the characteristic rhythmic skank of reggae music?

o.o1: Short chords on the weak beats
o.o2: Four beats on the bass drum per bar
o.o3: The melody sits ahead of the tempo
o.o4: Long chords on the first beat

music-quality-reggae-offbeat-001.e: In much reggae, guitar or keyboard marks the weak beats of the bar with short chords, often called skank. Together with bass and drums this gives the music its characteristic rhythmic bounce.

kz-rl1gew.p: How many strings does a violin have?
kz-rl1gew.e: The four strings are tuned in G, D, A and E.

kz-m6qvqx.p: What is the most common element in the universe?
kz-m6qvqx.e: About three quarters of all ordinary matter in the universe is hydrogen. Helium makes up most of the rest.

kz-lk0e59.p: Which blood type is the most common in Denmark?
kz-lk0e59.e: About 44 per cent of Danes have blood type A. Worldwide, O is the most common.

kz-1og27nv.p: What number does the Roman numeral L represent?
kz-1og27nv.e: L is 50, C is 100, D is 500 and M is 1,000.

kz-1okrxa0.p: How many time zones does China officially have?
kz-1okrxa0.e: China stretches across five geographical time zones, but the whole country follows Beijing time. In western China the sun can therefore rise at 10 a.m.

kz-1ad3y2q.p: What colour is the ‘black box’ on an aircraft?
kz-1ad3y2q.e: The aircraft’s flight recorder is painted a vivid orange so that it is easier to find in a wreck.

kz-sjahb1.p: What did the distress signal SOS originally stand for?
kz-sjahb1.e: SOS was chosen because its Morse code – three short, three long, three short – is easy to recognise. The meanings were invented afterwards.

kz-1imqj3u.e: The Sargasso Sea lies in the middle of the Atlantic and is bounded only by ocean currents. It is where the European eel spawns.

kz-u6uzsb.p: Which metal is liquid at room temperature?
kz-u6uzsb.e: Mercury melts at minus 39 degrees and is the only metal that is liquid at ordinary room temperature.

kz-1rua9lp.p: How many zeros are there in a billion?
kz-1rua9lp.e: A billion is a thousand million: 1,000,000,000. In English the same number is called “a billion”.

kz-1b9jxyd.p: What is the total number of pips on an ordinary die?
kz-1b9jxyd.e: 1 + 2 + 3 + 4 + 5 + 6 = 21. Two opposite faces always add up to 7.

kz-18bxoe8.p: What do the pips on two opposite faces of a die always add up to?
kz-18bxoe8.e: 1 is opposite 6, 2 is opposite 5 and 3 is opposite 4.

kz-1xfxl38.p: What is the chemical symbol for silver?
kz-1xfxl38.e: Ag comes from the Latin argentum. It also gave its name to Argentina – “land of silver”.

kz-upo8nw.p: Which element is named after Copenhagen?
kz-upo8nw.e: Hafnium was discovered at the Niels Bohr Institute in 1923 and is named after Hafnia, the Latin name for Copenhagen. Holmium is named after Stockholm.

kz-1b0jsm2.p: Four elements are named after the same small Swedish town. Which one?
kz-1b0jsm2.e: Yttrium, ytterbium, terbium and erbium are all named after Ytterby in the Stockholm archipelago, where the minerals were found in a quarry.

kz-1v5upzb.p: How many cards are there in a standard deck of playing cards without jokers?
kz-1v5upzb.e: Four suits with 13 cards each make 52.

kz-dnfd4b.p: Which naturally occurring mineral is the hardest?
kz-dnfd4b.e: Diamond has a hardness of 10 on the Mohs scale. Corundum – which rubies and sapphires consist of – is second with 9.

kz-1ijn0wr.p: How many court cards are there in a standard deck of playing cards?
kz-1ijn0wr.e: Jacks, queens and kings in four suits make 12 court cards.

kz-ee8ik4.p: How many faces does a dodecahedron have?
kz-ee8ik4.e: Dodeka is Greek for twelve. An icosahedron has 20 faces and is the shape many role-playing dice have.

kz-akg7y6.p: True or false: A tomato is botanically a fruit.
kz-akg7y6.e: The tomato develops from the flower’s ovary and contains seeds. In the kitchen it is nonetheless regarded as a vegetable.

kz-1bfx5hz.p: True or false: There are more possible chess games than atoms in the observable universe.
kz-1bfx5hz.e: The number of possible games is estimated at around 10 to the power of 120. The atoms in the observable universe number “only” around 10 to the power of 80.

kz-shddh5.p: How many bones does a hand have, including the wrist?
kz-shddh5.e: Eight carpal bones, five metacarpal bones and 14 phalanges. Hands and feet together contain more than half of the body’s bones.

kz-3uu7py.p: Which of these animals is not a marsupial?
kz-3uu7py.e: The platypus is a monotreme that lays eggs. The other three give birth to small young that finish growing in a pouch.

kz-1ni5s31.p: According to legend, the Dannebrog fell from the sky in 1219. In which present-day country did this happen?
kz-1ni5s31.e: It is said to have happened during Valdemar Sejr’s battle at Lyndanisse, now Tallinn. The name of the city means “the Danes’ castle”.

kz-zzxkta.p: How many municipalities did Denmark get from the 2007 municipal reform?
kz-zzxkta.e: The reform merged 271 municipalities into 98 and replaced the counties with five regions.

kz-1bps9ui.p: Which two bodies of water meet at Grenen?
kz-1bps9ui.e: At Denmark’s northern tip you can stand with one foot in each sea and watch the waves meet.

kz-k26l2t.p: In which town is the cathedral where most Danish kings and queens are buried?
kz-k26l2t.e: Roskilde Cathedral contains around 40 royal tombs and is on UNESCO’s World Heritage List.

kz-t4wxwu.p: Which king boasts on the great Jelling Stone of having made the Danes Christian?
kz-t4wxwu.e: The stone, from around the year 965, is called Denmark’s baptism certificate. The small Jelling Stone was raised by Harald’s father, Gorm the Old.

kz-kmzmoq.p: Which wireless technology is named after a Danish Viking king?
kz-kmzmoq.e: Harald Bluetooth united Denmark, just as the technology was meant to unite devices. The logo is his initials written in runes.

kz-19w3lbj.p: Who was Denmark’s last absolute monarch?
kz-19w3lbj.e: Frederick VII signed the Danish Constitution in 1849, thereby abolishing his own absolute monarchy.

kz-1mb4aca.e: Himmelbjerget was long considered Denmark’s highest point. Today we know that Møllehøj is just under 24 metres higher.

kz-kncbza.p: Which town is regarded as Denmark’s oldest?
kz-kncbza.e: Archaeologists have found traces of a market place in Ribe dating from the beginning of the 700s.

kz-4ye2g7.p: In which year did Denmark sell the Danish West Indies to the USA?
kz-4ye2g7.e: The USA paid 25 million dollars in gold for the islands, which are today called the U.S. Virgin Islands.

kz-1swxbx1.p: Which Danish castle is the setting for Shakespeare’s “Hamlet”?
kz-1swxbx1.e: Shakespeare called the castle Elsinore after Helsingør. There is nothing to suggest that he ever visited it himself.

kz-x9wokg.p: How many times has Denmark won the Eurovision Song Contest?
kz-x9wokg.e: Grethe and Jørgen Ingmann in 1963, Brødrene Olsen in 2000 and Emmelie de Forest in 2013.

kz-11xhorf.e: The mute swan won a viewers’ vote in 1984 and replaced the skylark. The choice fitted nicely with H.C. Andersen’s The Ugly Duckling.

kz-qtz11.p: Which Danish city opened the country’s first modern light rail in 2017?
kz-qtz11.e: Odense followed in 2022. Aalborg dropped its light rail and instead got a long electric bus line.

kz-t77a4q.p: What is the capital of the Faroe Islands?
kz-t77a4q.e: Tórshavn means Thor’s harbour. With around 14,000 inhabitants it is one of the world’s smallest capitals.

kz-1dag0a1.p: What is the most common surname in Denmark?
kz-1dag0a1.e: Nielsen has been at the top since 2016. Jensen is second and Hansen third.

kz-xodl16.p: What share of Denmark’s land area is farmland?
kz-xodl16.e: Denmark is one of the most cultivated countries in the world. By comparison, forest covers about 15 per cent.

kz-1hbbkuw.p: True or false: Nowhere in Denmark is more than about 50 kilometres from the sea.
kz-1hbbkuw.e: The point furthest from the coast is found in central Jutland – just over 50 kilometres from the nearest coast.

kz-rue1vh.p: Which Danish amusement park opened first?
kz-rue1vh.e: Bakken dates from 1583 and is the world’s oldest amusement park. Tivoli opened in 1843, Legoland in 1968.

kz-4cr662.p: In which year did Danish women gain the right to vote in elections to the Rigsdag?
kz-4cr662.e: The 1915 constitutional amendment gave women and servants the right to vote. Women had been able to vote in municipal elections since 1908.

kz-bexekg.p: In which year was the voting age lowered to 18?
kz-bexekg.e: The voting age was lowered in several steps and was reduced to 18 in 1978.

kz-1409kt8.p: What share of the vote does a party normally need to get into the Folketing (the Danish parliament)?
kz-1409kt8.e: Denmark’s electoral threshold is among the lowest in Europe. In Sweden it is 4 per cent and in Germany 5.

kz-1rxv2r9.p: How many of the Folketing’s 179 members are elected in the Faroe Islands and Greenland combined?
kz-1rxv2r9.e: Two are elected in the Faroe Islands and two in Greenland. In close elections the North Atlantic seats can decide the majority.

kz-169h5ue.p: In which year was the Landsting (the upper house) abolished, leaving the Folketing on its own?
kz-169h5ue.e: The same constitutional amendment lowered the voting age and made it possible for a woman to inherit the throne.

kz-d0wsk0.p: What did the Act of Succession of 1953 make possible?

o.o1: A woman could inherit the throne
o.o3: The Folketing could choose the monarch
o.o4: The throne could pass to a son-in-law

kz-d0wsk0.e: Without the change, the throne would have passed to Frederick IX’s brother, Prince Knud, instead of to Margrethe.

kz-1dr9zpw.p: Who became Denmark’s first female prime minister?
kz-1dr9zpw.e: Helle Thorning-Schmidt was prime minister from 2011 to 2015.

kz-169hc6k.p: Who became Denmark’s first female minister in 1924?
kz-169hc6k.e: Nina Bang became Minister for Education in Stauning’s first government – and one of the very first female ministers in the world.

kz-15fwuuk.p: What is it called when a majority in the Folketing forces a minister to resign?
kz-15fwuuk.e: Under section 15 of the Danish Constitution, no minister can remain in office once the Folketing has expressed no confidence in them.

kz-a86y5o.p: Which prime minister served the longest in the 20th century?
kz-a86y5o.e: Stauning was prime minister for more than 15 years, from 1924 to 1926 and again from 1929 until his death in 1942.

kz-e38ubn.p: Which election slogan from 1935 has stayed in Danish politics?
kz-e38ubn.e: The poster gave the Social Democrats 46 per cent of the vote – the party’s best result ever.

kz-1t58o2j.p: What is the term for the negotiations over who is to form a government after an election?
kz-1t58o2j.e: The parties nominate a negotiator to the monarch. Under Margrethe II it was called a “queen’s round”.

kz-1vs0la8.p: In which election year did the number of parties in the Folketing double from five to ten?
kz-1vs0la8.e: More than one in three voters switched party, and the Progress Party became at once the second-largest party in the Folketing.

kz-1boiydi.p: Who founded the Progress Party after telling TV viewers that he paid zero kroner in tax?
kz-1boiydi.e: In 1971 Glistrup compared tax refusers with resistance fighters. Two years later his party won 28 seats.

kz-1rdzb3s.p: Which affair brought down Poul Schlüter’s government in 1993?
kz-1rdzb3s.e: An inquiry showed that the Minister of Justice had unlawfully halted family reunifications for Tamil refugees.

kz-49srkg.p: Who can be brought before the High Court of the Realm (Rigsretten)?
kz-49srkg.e: The High Court of the Realm hears cases on ministers’ conduct in office. It has been used only six times since 1849.

kz-fl82mp.p: How many signatures must a citizens’ initiative have to be considered by the Folketing?
kz-fl82mp.e: The scheme was introduced in 2018. Supporters must collect the signatures within 180 days.

kz-1gidokm.p: Which of Denmark’s EU opt-outs was abolished in a referendum in 2022?
kz-1gidokm.e: Just under 67 per cent voted yes to abolish it, a few months after Russia’s invasion of Ukraine.

kz-28356d.p: In which year did Danish voters reject the euro?
kz-28356d.e: 53 per cent voted no. The krone is nonetheless pegged to the euro through a fixed-rate policy.

kz-m3usni.p: How many times has the Danish Constitution been amended since 1849?
kz-m3usni.e: In 1866, 1915, 1920 and 1953. It is one of the world’s most difficult constitutions to amend.

kz-1j8exej.p: What share of all eligible voters must at least vote yes before the Danish Constitution can be amended?
kz-1j8exej.e: It is not enough to have a majority of the votes cast. The requirement makes low turnout an ally of the no side.

kz-hwjldk.p: Which palace is home to the Folketing, the Supreme Court and the Prime Minister’s Office?
kz-hwjldk.e: Christiansborg is the only place in the world where the legislative, executive and judicial powers share the same roof.

kz-bn51pi.p: Which party is list B on the ballot paper?
kz-bn51pi.e: The Social Democrats have A, the Conservatives C and SF the letter F.

kz-1mmdxd0.p: Who became prime minister of the Liberation government in May 1945?
kz-1mmdxd0.e: The government consisted of equal parts politicians and resistance members, and sat until the election that October.

kz-nandeh.p: What triggered the Easter Crisis of 1920?
kz-nandeh.e: Christian X dismissed the Zahle government because he wanted Flensburg brought home. The threat of a general strike made him back down – and since then no monarch has interfered in that way.

kz-10c8i77.p: What is the name of the political festival held every summer in Allinge on Bornholm?
kz-10c8i77.e: Folkemødet is inspired by the Swedish Almedalsveckan on Gotland and was first held in 2011.

kz-14imxm4.p: How many stars are there on the EU flag?
kz-14imxm4.e: The number has never followed the number of member states. The twelve stars stand for perfection and unity.

kz-1b7cks7.p: Which article of the NATO treaty says that an attack on one member is an attack on all?
kz-1b7cks7.e: The musketeers’ oath is the very heart of the alliance.

kz-6fkwiy.p: NATO’s Article 5 has been invoked only once. When?

o.o2: During the Cuban Missile Crisis in 1962
o.o4: After the annexation of Crimea in 2014

kz-6fkwiy.e: The day after the terrorist attacks on the USA, the allies declared that the attack was an attack on them all.

kz-1ikpdp3.p: Which two Nordic countries became members of NATO in 2023 and 2024?
kz-1ikpdp3.e: Russia’s invasion of Ukraine led both countries to give up decades of alliance freedom.

kz-94i9a4.p: Which of these countries was not among the founders of the EU’s predecessor in 1951?
kz-94i9a4.e: The European Coal and Steel Community was founded by France, West Germany, Italy and the Benelux countries. The British only joined in 1973.

kz-1rpgkwv.p: In which year did Denmark become a member of the EEC?
kz-1rpgkwv.e: Denmark joined together with the United Kingdom and Ireland. Norway voted no.

kz-9dqggp.p: How many members does the US Senate have?
kz-9dqggp.e: Each state has two senators regardless of its size. The House of Representatives has 435 members.

kz-8flc5z.p: How many electoral votes must a candidate have to win the US presidential election?
kz-8flc5z.e: There are 538 electors in total, so 270 is the smallest majority.

kz-181rk34.p: What is the name of Germany’s parliament?
kz-181rk34.e: The Bundestag meets in the Reichstag building in Berlin – hence the confusion.

kz-st13mo.p: Which country has the world’s oldest parliament, founded around the year 930?
kz-st13mo.e: The Althing met under the open sky at Thingvellir. Today it is based in Reykjavík.

kz-1rcgd53.p: Who was the last leader of the Soviet Union?
kz-1rcgd53.e: Gorbachev resigned on Christmas Day 1991, and the Soviet Union ceased to exist the day after.

kz-1upkfeu.p: What is the name of the 1998 agreement that brought peace to Northern Ireland?
kz-1upkfeu.e: The agreement was concluded on Good Friday and ended three decades of conflict that cost more than 3,500 people their lives.

kz-1bvv0hw.p: Which of these countries is not a member of the G7?
kz-1bvv0hw.e: The G7 consists of the USA, Canada, Japan, Germany, France, Italy and the United Kingdom.

kz-1mn13yv.p: Which UN Secretary-General was killed in a plane crash in 1961?
kz-1mn13yv.e: The Swede was on his way to peace negotiations in the Congo. He is the only one to have received the Nobel Peace Prize after his death.

kz-1di039u.p: In which city is the European Central Bank located?
kz-1di039u.e: The bank manages monetary policy for the euro countries from a high-rise building by the River Main.

kz-17grijt.p: What was the dividing line between east and west in Europe during the Cold War called?
kz-17grijt.e: Winston Churchill made the expression famous in a speech in 1946.

kz-svfy1v.p: Which country is the world’s largest democracy measured by number of voters?
kz-svfy1v.e: An Indian parliamentary election has close to one billion eligible voters and stretches over several weeks.

kz-1772fdi.p: Which year did the UN adopt the Universal Declaration of Human Rights?
kz-1772fdi.e: The declaration was adopted in Paris on 10 December, which has since become Human Rights Day.

kz-1b94snz.p: Which US president resigned after the Watergate scandal?
kz-1b94snz.e: Nixon stepped down in 1974 and is the only US president to have resigned.

kz-1hk3dym.p: What is Schengen, which gave its name to the agreement on open borders?
kz-1hk3dym.e: The agreement was signed in 1985 on a ship on the Moselle, right where Luxembourg, Germany and France meet.

kz-1fy1vqy.p: Which small state has been guarded by the Swiss Guard since 1506?
kz-1fy1vqy.e: The guards must be Swiss Catholics. Their striped uniforms are, however, only about a hundred years old.

kz-144ecec.p: True or false: Switzerland only became a member of the UN in 2002.
kz-144ecec.e: The UN has a large European office in Geneva, but the Swiss only voted yes to membership in a 2002 referendum.

kz-3u3f5c.e: The Red Cross was founded in 1863, the League of Nations in 1920, the UN in 1945 and NATO in 1949.

kz-115xbip.p: How long did the Hundred Years’ War between England and France last?
kz-115xbip.e: The war lasted from 1337 to 1453 – with long pauses along the way.

kz-6y76x7.p: History’s shortest war lasted less than an hour in 1896. Who were the British fighting?
kz-6y76x7.e: The sultan’s palace was shelled from the harbour, and after about 40 minutes the war was over.

kz-1hicogh.p: True or false: Cleopatra lived closer in time to the Moon landing than to the building of the Great Pyramid of Khufu.
kz-1hicogh.e: The pyramid was completed around 2560 BC. Cleopatra died in 30 BC – around 2,500 years later, but only about 2,000 years before Apollo 11.

kz-1w3bihh.p: True or false: The University of Oxford is older than the Aztec empire.
kz-1w3bihh.e: Teaching took place in Oxford in 1096. The Aztecs first founded their capital, Tenochtitlan, in 1325.

kz-5ojkw6.p: True or false: Vikings wore helmets with horns in battle.
kz-5ojkw6.e: No Viking helmet with horns has ever been found. The idea comes from 19th-century paintings and opera costumes.

kz-1wfv8vu.p: True or false: Napoleon was unusually short.
kz-1wfv8vu.e: He was about 1.68 metres tall – slightly above the average for French men at the time. The myth stems from British caricatures and confusion over French inches.

kz-phabp7.p: Which city was buried under ash when Vesuvius erupted in AD 79?
kz-phabp7.e: The ash preserved the city so well that graffiti on the walls can still be read today.

kz-10q2cdq.p: What did the Vikings call the land in North America that Leif the Lucky found?
kz-10q2cdq.e: The settlement at L’Anse aux Meadows on Newfoundland shows that Norse people reached America around the year 1000 – almost 500 years before Columbus.

kz-dusdgp.p: Who was the first European to find the sea route to India around Africa?
kz-dusdgp.e: Da Gama reached Calicut in 1498. Dias had rounded the Cape of Good Hope ten years earlier, but turned back.

kz-802g9j.p: Who brought the first circumnavigation to completion after Magellan had been killed on the way?
kz-802g9j.e: Of five ships and about 270 men, only one ship and 18 men returned to Spain in 1522.

kz-yif33w.p: In which year did the Allies land in Normandy on D-Day?
kz-yif33w.e: On 6 June 1944 around 156,000 soldiers landed on five beaches.

kz-omqbu4.p: On which date was Denmark occupied by Germany?
kz-omqbu4.e: The occupation lasted until 5 May 1945 – though on Bornholm it lasted a year longer, under Soviet troops.

kz-1oo1frh.p: What happened in Denmark on 29 August 1943?
kz-1oo1frh.e: The government refused to introduce the death penalty for sabotage and stopped functioning. On the same day the navy scuttled its own ships.

kz-qbf8wq.p: How many Danish Jews were ferried to safety in Sweden in October 1943?
kz-qbf8wq.e: Most of them crossed the Øresund in fishing boats after a German diplomat had warned of the planned operation.

kz-yzhx2j.p: Who did Denmark lose the 1864 war to?
kz-yzhx2j.e: The defeat at Dybbøl cost Schleswig, Holstein and Lauenburg.

kz-1pvzytj.p: In which year did Southern Jutland become part of Denmark again?
kz-1pvzytj.e: After Germany’s defeat in the First World War, two referendums decided where the border would run.

kz-1i6ppbr.p: Which king rode over the old border on a white horse at the Reunification (Genforeningen)?
kz-1i6ppbr.e: The picture from 10 July 1920 is one of the most famous in Danish history. According to rumour, the horse had been whitewashed to look whiter than it really was.

kz-1a323uv.p: Who united Denmark, Norway and Sweden in the Kalmar Union in 1397?
kz-1a323uv.e: Margaret was never crowned queen but ruled all three realms as “lady and lord with full powers”.

kz-1xbr49v.p: In which year did Denmark have to cede Norway?
kz-1xbr49v.e: Denmark had sided with Napoleon and lost. Norway went to Sweden, while Iceland, the Faroe Islands and Greenland stayed with Denmark.

kz-1vqkurg.p: Who bombarded Copenhagen in 1807 and sailed away with the Danish fleet?
kz-1vqkurg.e: Three nights of bombardment destroyed large parts of the city. The British wanted to prevent the fleet from falling into Napoleon’s hands.

kz-6em8ti.p: In which year was the stavnsbånd (the law binding peasants to their parish) abolished?
kz-6em8ti.e: The Liberty Monument (Frihedsstøtten) at Copenhagen Central Station was raised to commemorate the reform that gave peasants the right to move.

kz-zf56zl.p: Which German doctor effectively ruled Denmark on behalf of the insane King Christian VII?
kz-zf56zl.e: Struensee issued over a thousand cabinet orders in about 13 months, fathered a child with the queen and was executed in 1772.

kz-2i4dke.p: Which Roman emperor gave his name to the wall across northern England?
kz-2i4dke.e: The wall was 117 kilometres long and marked the northern frontier of the Roman Empire.

kz-jyumxw.p: What was history’s largest contiguous land empire?
kz-jyumxw.e: At its height in the 1200s it stretched from Korea to Hungary. The British Empire was larger, but spread across the whole globe.

kz-1b7grsv.p: In which year did the Ottomans conquer Constantinople?
kz-1b7grsv.e: The fall of the city marks the end of the Byzantine Empire – and for many historians also the end of the Middle Ages.

kz-uf3gcm.p: What was the name of the ship that carried the English pilgrims to America in 1620?
kz-uf3gcm.e: The ship landed at Cape Cod with 102 passengers after 66 days at sea.

kz-u9wgt0.p: Which country was the first in the world to give women the vote in national elections?
kz-u9wgt0.e: It happened in 1893. Finland became the first country in Europe to do so in 1906.

kz-xgcbuk.p: Which pharaoh’s tomb did Howard Carter find almost untouched in 1922?
kz-xgcbuk.e: The tomb contained over 5,000 objects, including the famous golden death mask.

kz-14gsjss.p: Which stone made it possible to decipher Egyptian hieroglyphs?
kz-14gsjss.e: The stone carries the same text in three scripts, including Greek, which researchers could already read.

kz-kc9sf6.p: Hitler promised a thousand-year Reich. How many years did the Third Reich actually last?
kz-kc9sf6.e: From the seizure of power in January 1933 to the capitulation in May 1945.

kz-17caq14.p: Which Swedish warship sank on its maiden voyage in 1628 after just over a kilometre of sailing?
kz-17caq14.e: The ship was too narrow and too high. It was raised in 1961 and is today Scandinavia’s most visited museum.

kz-2nlk99.p: Which Danish astronomer built the Uraniborg observatory on Hven?
kz-2nlk99.e: Tycho Brahe’s measurements were the most precise ever made without a telescope. He also, incidentally, lost part of his nose in a duel.

kz-zqgm93.p: What did Ole Rømer show for the first time in 1676?
kz-zqgm93.e: He discovered that the eclipses of Jupiter’s moon Io occurred later when the Earth was farthest away, so light must take time to make the journey.

kz-ay9es6.p: Which city was the capital of the Inca Empire?
kz-ay9es6.e: Cusco in modern Peru means “navel of the world” in Quechua. Tenochtitlan was the capital of the Aztecs.

kz-njmcd1.p: What was the secret American plan that led to the atomic bomb?
kz-njmcd1.e: The project employed tens of thousands of people. Niels Bohr contributed as an adviser after fleeing Denmark.

kz-t50jiz.p: Put the events in order – oldest first.
kz-t50jiz.e: The plague raged from 1347, Columbus sailed in 1492, the revolution broke out in 1789 and Waterloo was fought in 1815.

kz-10ow2ub.p: Put the Danish kings in order – oldest first.
kz-10ow2ub.e: Gorm died around 958, Cnut reigned from 1018, Valdemar Sejr from 1202 and Christian IV from 1588.

kz-145n1co.p: Which of these was founded first?
kz-145n1co.e: The university dates from 1479, the National Bank from 1818, Tivoli from 1843 and Carlsberg from 1847.

kz-r6h0uw.p: What is the capital of Australia?
kz-r6h0uw.e: Sydney and Melbourne could not agree on which should be the capital. The compromise was to build an entirely new city between them.

kz-sguqi2.p: What is the capital of Turkey?
kz-sguqi2.e: In 1923 Atatürk moved the capital away from Istanbul to the middle of the country.

kz-16o8jqf.p: What is the capital of Brazil?
kz-16o8jqf.e: Brasília was built from scratch in under four years and inaugurated in 1960. Seen from the air, the city plan looks like an aeroplane.

kz-155xq7k.p: How many capitals does South Africa have?
kz-155xq7k.e: The government sits in Pretoria, parliament in Cape Town and the Supreme Court of Appeal in Bloemfontein.

kz-1fbk17j.p: What is the capital of Kazakhstan?
kz-1fbk17j.e: The city was called Nur-Sultan from 2019 to 2022, but then got its old name back. Astana simply means “capital”.

kz-10ejtjb.p: What is the capital of New Zealand?
kz-10ejtjb.e: Wellington is the southernmost capital of an independent country in the world.

kz-1l8f5u8.p: What is the capital of Morocco?
kz-1l8f5u8.e: Casablanca is far larger, but the king and government are based in Rabat.

kz-yp2kvr.p: What is the capital of Myanmar?
kz-yp2kvr.e: In 2005 the military government suddenly moved the capital to a newly built city in the middle of the country, with ten-lane, almost empty roads.

kz-12o4jff.p: What is the capital of Nigeria?
kz-12o4jff.e: Abuja replaced Lagos in 1991. It was placed in the middle of the country so as not to belong to any of the major ethnic groups.

kz-1eknlhb.p: What is the capital of Pakistan?
kz-1eknlhb.e: Islamabad was built in the 1960s to replace Karachi.

kz-1c23nts.p: What is the capital of Vietnam?
kz-1c23nts.e: Ho Chi Minh City – formerly Saigon – is larger, but Hanoi in the north has been the capital since reunification in 1976.

kz-d7y1vq.e: The Seine divides the city into the Right Bank and the Left Bank – Rive Droite and Rive Gauche.

kz-1ua2x0q.p: What is the world’s largest desert?
kz-1ua2x0q.e: A desert is defined by how little precipitation falls, not by heat. Antarctica is one and a half times the size of the Sahara.

kz-ux99an.p: Which country has the most time zones when overseas territories are counted?
kz-ux99an.e: Including areas from French Polynesia to New Caledonia, France reaches 12 time zones. Russia has 11.

kz-hl27ed.p: What is the world’s smallest independent state?
kz-hl27ed.e: Vatican City covers 0.44 square kilometres – less than Fælledparken in Copenhagen.

kz-1k4emjo.p: Which two countries are surrounded by landlocked countries?
kz-1k4emjo.e: From there you must cross at least two borders to reach the sea.

kz-1ted41x.p: Which country has the most islands in the world?
kz-1ted41x.e: Sweden has over 260,000 islands when you count all the small islets. Indonesia has only about 17,000.

kz-1hqq11v.p: Which African country has the largest population?
kz-1hqq11v.e: Nigeria has more than 220 million inhabitants and is Africa’s most populous country.

kz-1hnmbj7.p: What is Europe's highest mountain when the Caucasus is included?
kz-1hnmbj7.e: Elbrus in Russia is 5,642 metres. Mont Blanc, at 4,806 metres, is the highest in the Alps.

kz-v64rk6.p: In which country is the Inca city of Machu Picchu located?
kz-v64rk6.e: The city lies 2,400 metres up in the Andes and was unknown to the outside world until 1911.

kz-axs8s3.p: Which major city lies in both Europe and Asia?
kz-axs8s3.e: The Bosphorus strait divides the city into a European and an Asian part.

kz-rbffy1.p: How far below sea level is the shore of the Dead Sea?
kz-rbffy1.e: It is the lowest place on the Earth's land surface – and the lake sinks by about a metre a year.

kz-ie4v34.e: Denmark, Poland, Czechia, Austria, Switzerland, France, Luxembourg, Belgium and the Netherlands.

kz-18r0ctr.p: What is the name of the world's deepest lake?
kz-18r0ctr.e: Lake Baikal in Siberia is over 1,600 metres deep and holds a fifth of the planet's liquid fresh water.

kz-184wqkk.p: Where is the world's highest waterfall, Angel Falls?
