kz-184wqkk.e: The water falls 979 metres. The falls are named after the pilot Jimmie Angel, who landed his plane on top of them in 1937.

kz-owbx6f.p: Which country does Easter Island belong to?
kz-owbx6f.e: The island lies over 3,500 kilometres from the Chilean coast and is known for its nearly 900 moai statues.

kz-1uu73hy.p: Greenland is the world's largest island. Which is the second largest?
kz-1uu73hy.e: New Guinea is shared between Indonesia and Papua New Guinea. Borneo is number three and Madagascar number four.

kz-9q36rg.p: What is the strait between Asia and North America called?
kz-9q36rg.e: The strait is named after the Dane Vitus Bering, who sailed through it in Russian service in 1728.

kz-1ffmx1r.p: Which country was called Siam until 1939?
kz-1ffmx1r.e: Thailand means “land of the free”. It is the only country in Southeast Asia that has never been a colony.

kz-trv6ne.p: Which European capital lies at the mouth of the River Tagus?
kz-trv6ne.e: The Tagus is the longest river on the Iberian Peninsula and also flows past Toledo in Spain.

kz-1qd0uq8.p: Which country has Europe's longest coastline?
kz-1qd0uq8.e: With its fjords and islands, the Norwegian coastline runs to over 100,000 kilometres – enough to go two and a half times around the Earth.

kz-1ys3pum.p: Which Pacific island nation lies in all four hemispheres?
kz-1ys3pum.e: The island nation in the Pacific stretches across both the equator and the date line.

kz-pyepet.p: Which country has the most pyramids in the world?
kz-pyepet.e: The Nubian kings in what is now Sudan built over 200 pyramids – roughly twice as many as there are in Egypt.

kz-165i0p8.p: True or false: Africa is the only continent that lies in all four hemispheres.
kz-165i0p8.e: Both the equator and the prime meridian run through Africa.

kz-1j65hlw.p: True or false: Reykjavik lies further north than Helsinki.
kz-1j65hlw.e: Reykjavik lies at 64 degrees north and is the world's northernmost capital of an independent country. Helsinki lies at 60 degrees.

kz-1ezes4j.p: Put the world's oceans in order by size – largest first.
kz-1ezes4j.e: The Pacific Ocean alone is larger than all of the Earth's land areas combined.

kz-9ht8l7.p: Which of these countries does not use the euro as its currency?
kz-9ht8l7.e: Czechia still uses the koruna. Slovakia adopted the euro in 2009, Estonia in 2011 and Croatia in 2023.

kz-rok108.p: Which of these countries does not lie on the Mediterranean?
kz-rok108.e: The whole of Portugal's coastline faces the Atlantic Ocean.

kz-15knx8a.p: Which gas do plants take from the air during photosynthesis?
kz-15knx8a.e: Plants use carbon dioxide, water and sunlight to make sugar – and release oxygen as a by-product.

kz-h9opeh.p: Which gas is most abundant in the air we breathe?
kz-h9opeh.e: Air consists of about 78 per cent nitrogen and 21 per cent oxygen. Carbon dioxide makes up only around 0.04 per cent.

kz-lqmvmh.p: What is the pH value of pure water?
kz-lqmvmh.e: 7 is neutral. Lower numbers are acidic and higher ones alkaline – and the scale is logarithmic, so each step is a factor of ten.

kz-a8c0qi.p: At what temperature do the Celsius and Fahrenheit scales show the same number?
kz-a8c0qi.e: Minus 40 is the only point at which the two scales cross each other.

kz-277r6r.p: What is absolute zero in degrees Celsius?
kz-277r6r.e: Nothing can be colder. On the kelvin scale it is 0 K – and minus 459.67 is the same temperature in Fahrenheit.

kz-1hftbd8.p: What is a diamond made of?
kz-1hftbd8.e: A diamond and the graphite in a pencil are both pure carbon. The difference lies solely in how the atoms are bonded together.

kz-1ccgpwg.e: A hydrogen atom has only one proton and one electron, and is the lightest of all elements.

kz-4o8bd6.p: Which Danish physicist won the Nobel Prize in 1922 for his atomic model?
kz-4o8bd6.e: Bohr described the electrons as bound to fixed orbits around the nucleus. His son Aage won the prize himself in 1975.

kz-5bl1jd.p: What did H.C. Ørsted discover in 1820?

o.o1: That an electric current affects a magnetic needle
o.o4: That blood has a circulatory system

kz-5bl1jd.e: Electromagnetism was discovered during a lecture in Copenhagen and is the basis for everything from electric motors to loudspeakers.

kz-1ln9deh.p: How fast does light travel in a vacuum?
kz-1ln9deh.e: At that speed, light travels seven and a half times around the Earth in one second.

kz-1dr4cdj.p: Which of these is not one of the four bases in DNA?
kz-1dr4cdj.e: DNA uses thymine as its fourth base. Uracil is found in RNA instead.

kz-x7abst.p: What does the half-life tell you about a radioactive substance?

o.o1: How long it takes for half of it to decay
o.o2: How long the substance is dangerous
o.o4: How long half the energy lasts

kz-x7abst.e: Carbon-14 has a half-life of 5,730 years, which makes it well suited to dating archaeological finds.

kz-1xs2zq4.p: What are animals called that keep a constant body temperature?
kz-1xs2zq4.e: Mammals and birds are warm-blooded. Reptiles, amphibians and fish are cold-blooded and follow the temperature of their surroundings.

kz-tl1mbt.p: What is the rarest naturally occurring element in the Earth's crust?
kz-tl1mbt.e: At any one time, there are less than 30 grams of astatine in the whole of the Earth's crust, because it decays within hours.

kz-3em9k3.p: Why does your voice sound high when you breathe in helium?

o.o1: Sound travels faster in the gas
o.o2: The gas tightens the vocal cords
o.o3: The gas thins the air in the lungs

kz-3em9k3.e: The vocal cords vibrate as normal, but in the light gas the high overtones are amplified in the throat.

kz-k3q2es.e: Dry ice is minus 78 degrees and does not melt – it goes straight from solid to gas.

kz-1kwa9qm.p: Which element is the only non-metal that is liquid at room temperature?
kz-1kwa9qm.e: Bromine is a reddish-brown, foul-smelling liquid. The name comes from the Greek word for stench.

kz-ktvmab.p: True or false: A lightning bolt is hotter than the surface of the Sun.
kz-ktvmab.e: The air in a lightning channel reaches around 30,000 degrees – five times as hot as the surface of the Sun.

kz-12s5vzo.p: Put the units in order – smallest first.
kz-12s5vzo.e: There are a thousand nanometres in a micrometre and a thousand micrometres in a millimetre. A human hair is about 70 micrometres thick.

kz-gsim88.p: Which of these is not a noble gas?
kz-gsim88.e: Fluorine is a halogen and one of the most reactive elements there are. Noble gases barely react with anything.

kz-9zqvay.p: How long does sunlight take to reach Earth?
kz-9zqvay.e: Light travels almost 300,000 kilometres per second, but the Sun is 150 million kilometres away.

kz-zko1xc.p: Which planet has the most known moons?
kz-zko1xc.e: Saturn has overtaken Jupiter and now has well over a hundred confirmed moons.

kz-1xoyjlh.p: What is the name of the galaxy that is the Milky Way's nearest large neighbour?
kz-1xoyjlh.e: Andromeda lies 2.5 million light years away and is among the most distant things visible to the naked eye.

kz-1rhvrff.p: What is the hottest planet in the solar system?
kz-1rhvrff.e: Venus's dense atmosphere of carbon dioxide traps the heat, so its surface is around 465 degrees – hotter than Mercury, which is closer to the Sun.

kz-132ec4e.p: Who became the first Dane in space in 2015?
kz-132ec4e.e: Andreas Mogensen flew to the International Space Station in 2015 and in 2023 was commander of the station during his second mission.

kz-y4dwo6.p: What was the first living creature to orbit the Earth?
kz-y4dwo6.e: Laika was launched aboard Sputnik 2 in 1957. Unfortunately, she survived only a few hours.

kz-18hsqp3.p: How many people have walked on the Moon?
kz-18hsqp3.e: Twelve American astronauts set foot on the Moon between 1969 and 1972. Nobody has been there since.

kz-hagf52.p: Who stayed in orbit around the Moon while Armstrong and Aldrin walked on the surface?
kz-hagf52.e: Collins flew alone around the far side of the Moon without radio contact and has been called the loneliest human in history.

kz-9dv7ll.p: What is the point called from which nothing can escape a black hole?
kz-9dv7ll.e: Inside the event horizon you would have to travel faster than light to escape – and nothing can do that.

kz-zuy3no.p: What are Saturn's rings mainly made of?
kz-zuy3no.e: The rings consist of billions of lumps of ice, ranging in size from grains of sand to houses. They are up to 280,000 kilometres wide, but in many places only ten metres thick.

kz-bbfyps.p: Which man-made object is furthest from the Earth?
kz-bbfyps.e: The probe was launched in 1977 and left the Sun's magnetic bubble in 2012. Its signals take about a day to reach us.

kz-9jg030.p: What is the tallest known volcano in the solar system?
kz-9jg030.e: The volcano rises about 22 kilometres – more than twice as high as Mount Everest.

kz-1am5xzl.p: Which planet was found by calculation before anyone had seen it?
kz-1am5xzl.e: Irregularities in Uranus's orbit revealed that there must be a planet further out. In 1846 it was almost exactly where the calculations said it would be.

kz-1fw2977.p: True or false: The Sun makes up more than 99 per cent of the solar system's total mass.
kz-1fw2977.e: The Sun accounts for 99.86 per cent. Jupiter makes up most of the rest.

kz-97smrg.p: True or false: Space is completely silent because there is no air to carry sound.
kz-97smrg.e: Sound consists of pressure waves and requires a substance to travel through. The explosions in space films would in reality be silent.

kz-2of9ep.p: True or false: The Moon is moving away from the Earth by a few centimetres each year.
kz-2of9ep.e: Laser reflectors left by the Apollo missions show that the distance is increasing by about 3.8 centimetres a year.

kz-20qnq9.p: Put the planets in order by size – largest first.
kz-20qnq9.e: Jupiter could hold more than 1,300 Earths. Uranus is slightly larger than Neptune in diameter.

kz-64m9do.p: What does the abbreviation GPS stand for?
kz-64m9do.e: The system is run by the US military and was released for civilian use in the 1980s.

kz-mxgciw.p: How many bits are there in a byte?
kz-mxgciw.e: With eight bits, a byte can have 256 different values.

kz-g9lm72.p: Which Dane developed the programming language C++?
kz-g9lm72.e: Hejlsberg is behind C# and TypeScript, and Lerdorf created PHP – three of the world's most widely used languages have Danish originators.

kz-uk7hfo.p: Which programming language did Rasmus Lerdorf create in the 1990s?
kz-uk7hfo.e: PHP originally stood for Personal Home Page and still powers a large part of the world's websites.

o.o2: Computers double in price every 10 years
o.o3: Software takes up more space on fast PCs
o.o4: Internet traffic increases tenfold every 5 years

kz-k608hr.e: Intel co-founder Gordon Moore formulated the observation in 1965, and it held roughly for half a century.

o.o1: One of the first electronic computers

kz-b8w45k.e: The machine from 1945 weighed 27 tonnes and filled an entire room.

kz-12iahs9.p: Why are the letters on a QWERTY keyboard in the order they are?

o.o1: So the typewriter arms would not get stuck
o.o2: So the most used keys are in the middle
o.o3: So passwords are hard to spy on

kz-12iahs9.e: Frequently used letter pairs were spread apart so the typebars would not jam together. The layout from the 1870s has outlived the technology it was designed for.

kz-i75yl1.p: What was Denmark's first computer, from 1957?
kz-i75yl1.e: Dansk Aritmetisk Sekvens Kalkulator stood in a villa in Valby and became famous when it predicted the result of the 1960 Folketing election.

kz-f6187j.p: Which company developed the first commercial microprocessor in 1971?
kz-f6187j.e: The Intel 4004 had 2,300 transistors. A modern phone chip has many billions.

kz-12lxgxe.p: Who is regarded as the father of the theoretical computer and cracked the Enigma code?
kz-12lxgxe.e: Turing's work at Bletchley Park is estimated to have shortened the war by several years.

kz-ot96e9.p: What does a 3D printer typically use to build an object?

o.o1: Thin layers stacked on top of each other
o.o2: A mould that the material is poured into
o.o3: A block that is milled down

kz-ot96e9.e: The technique is called additive manufacturing, because the material is laid down layer by layer.

kz-7414b2.p: True or false: The first computer mouse was made of wood.
kz-7414b2.e: Douglas Engelbart demonstrated it in 1968. It had two metal wheels and one button.

kz-1w7m9yu.p: True or false: The computer that guided Apollo 11 to the Moon had less processing power than a modern calculator.
kz-1w7m9yu.e: The Apollo Guidance Computer had around 4 kilobytes of working memory.

kz-1r67wto.e: Alexander Bain patented an image telegraph in 1843 – over 30 years before Bell received a patent on the telephone.

kz-kitlxm.p: What does the symbol @ mean in an email address?
kz-kitlxm.e: Programmer Ray Tomlinson chose the at sign in 1971 because it could not be confused with part of a name.

kz-1pcrjjk.p: What was the predecessor of the internet, switched on in 1969?
kz-1pcrjjk.e: The first message was supposed to be “login”, but the system crashed after two letters.

kz-1fo8ubs.p: What is the job of the internet's DNS system?

o.o1: To translate names into IP addresses

kz-1fo8ubs.e: DNS is the internet's phone book. Without it, you would have to remember strings of numbers instead of names.

kz-1ve3brx.p: Which HTTP error code means that the page does not exist?
kz-1ve3brx.e: 200 means everything is fine, 301 means the page has moved, and 500 means the server has an internal error.

kz-estcvr.p: Which small island state earns millions from renting out its .tv internet domain?
kz-estcvr.e: Income from the domain has at times made up a noticeable share of the country's state budget.

kz-1e17tiy.p: What was the first item sold on eBay?
kz-1e17tiy.e: The buyer collected broken laser pointers and paid 14.83 dollars in 1995.

kz-30ud6w.p: What was Google's search engine called while it was still a university project?
kz-30ud6w.e: The name referred to the fact that it analysed the links pointing back to a page.

kz-9vun27.p: The chat program Slack began as an internal tool at a company that was actually making what?
kz-9vun27.e: The game Glitch was shut down in 2012, but the team's chat tool lived on and was later sold for 27.7 billion dollars.

o.o1: Fake messages that lure out data
o.o3: An attack that overloads a server

kz-sii8sm.e: The word is a respelling of “fishing”: scammers cast out bait and hope someone takes it.

kz-koyun3.p: What is the purpose of a CAPTCHA?

o.o1: To tell humans apart from programs
o.o4: To store a login in the browser

kz-koyun3.e: The acronym stands for a fully automated Turing test. The distorted letters have also helped digitise old books.

kz-tmpw9w.p: True or false: The internet and the World Wide Web are two words for the same thing.
kz-tmpw9w.e: The internet is the network of connected computers itself. The web is one of several services that run on top of it – like email.

kz-ugn9gm.e: Hotmail arrived in 1996, Google in 1998, Wikipedia in 2001 and Facebook in 2004.

kz-1f3f2yz.p: Which social media platform was launched first?
kz-1f3f2yz.e: LinkedIn opened in 2003, Facebook in 2004, YouTube in 2005 and Twitter in 2006.

kz-8eg8tc.p: What is the body's longest bone called?
kz-8eg8tc.e: The thigh bone makes up about a quarter of a person's height.

kz-1ary68c.p: What is the body's largest organ?
kz-1ary68c.e: The skin of an adult covers around two square metres and weighs several kilograms.

kz-2r23ap.p: How many chambers does the human heart have?
kz-2r23ap.e: Two atria and two ventricles. The right side pumps blood to the lungs, the left side to the rest of the body.

kz-e5bafu.p: How many teeth does an adult have with all wisdom teeth included?
kz-e5bafu.e: Children have 20 milk teeth. Many adults are missing one or more of the four wisdom teeth.

kz-1mu8vy2.p: What is the hardest material in the body?
kz-1mu8vy2.e: Enamel consists almost entirely of mineral – but it cannot regenerate once it has worn away.

kz-1hi23xc.p: Roughly how many litres of blood does an adult have?
kz-1hi23xc.e: At rest, the heart pumps the entire volume around the body roughly once a minute.

kz-15i0y10.p: Which part of the eye has no blood vessels and gets its oxygen directly from the air?
kz-15i0y10.e: That is why a cornea can be transplanted without the same risk of rejection as other organs.

kz-1izrwru.p: Which vitamin did sailors get scurvy from lacking?
kz-1izrwru.e: British sailors took lime juice against the disease – hence the nickname “limeys”.

kz-xtsnh3.p: What is the most common eye colour in the world?
kz-xtsnh3.e: Up to 80 per cent of the world's population has brown eyes. Green is the rarest, at around 2 per cent.

kz-5vpibn.p: Why do the veins on the wrist look blue?

o.o1: Red light penetrates deeper than blue
o.o3: The vein walls contain blue dye

kz-5vpibn.e: Blood is always red – darker without oxygen, brighter with it. The blue colour is an optical effect of how light travels through the skin.

kz-gj0rwq.p: Which Dane won the Nobel Prize for discovering how the smallest blood vessels are regulated?
kz-gj0rwq.e: Krogh received the prize in 1920. He and his wife Marie later brought insulin production to Denmark – the beginning of Novo Nordisk.

kz-15687fh.p: What happens when you “crack” your knuckles?

o.o1: Gas bubbles in the joint fluid collapse
o.o2: The cartilage rubs against the bone
o.o3: The tendons snap across the joint

kz-15687fh.e: The sound is harmless. One doctor cracked the knuckles of only one hand for 60 years and found no difference between the hands.

kz-1e45re6.p: True or false: We only use 10 per cent of our brains.
kz-1e45re6.e: Brain scans show activity across almost the whole brain over the course of a day – even while we sleep.

kz-vuf06g.p: True or false: Hair and nails continue to grow after death.
kz-vuf06g.e: The skin dries out and retracts, so hair and nails look longer. But they do not actually grow.

kz-ttz457.p: True or false: Most body heat is lost through the head.
kz-ttz457.e: The head does not give off more heat than the rest of the body in proportion to its size. The myth comes from a military experiment in which only the head was uncovered.

kz-1eko651.p: True or false: A human has the same number of neck vertebrae as a giraffe.
kz-1eko651.e: Almost all mammals have seven neck vertebrae. The giraffe's are just up to 25 centimetres long each.

kz-1c2w0qs.p: Roughly how many times does a heart beat in a day?
kz-1c2w0qs.e: At 70 beats a minute, that adds up to around 100,000 beats a day – and three billion over a lifetime.

kz-xwgdc0.p: What does the ozone layer protect the Earth from?
kz-xwgdc0.e: The layer lies 15–35 kilometres up and is healing now that the ozone-depleting CFC gases have been banned.

kz-1kwhsxw.p: Which agreement from 1987 banned the gases that break down the ozone layer?
kz-1kwhsxw.e: The agreement is regarded as history's most successful environmental agreement and has been ratified by all the world's countries.

kz-a2231r.p: How much of the Earth's water is fresh water?
kz-a2231r.e: And most of the fresh water is locked up in ice and glaciers. Less than one per cent is accessible in lakes, rivers and groundwater.

kz-189boil.p: Which energy source provides the most electricity in Denmark?
kz-189boil.e: In good years, wind turbines cover more than half of Danish electricity consumption.

kz-rd7qaf.p: Which island has produced more renewable energy than it uses itself since 2007?
kz-rd7qaf.e: Samsø was designated Denmark's renewable energy island in 1997 and reached the goal within ten years, partly through wind turbines owned by the islanders themselves.

kz-vsbxim.p: What is methane best known for in a climate context?

o.o1: It warms far more than CO₂ per tonne
o.o2: It breaks down the ozone layer over the poles
o.o4: It blocks sunlight like a shade

kz-vsbxim.e: Over 20 years, methane is about 80 times as potent a greenhouse gas as CO₂. It comes from cows, rice paddies and leaking gas pipes, among other sources.

o.o1: Ground that is frozen all year round
o.o2: Ice that covers the sea in winter
o.o3: Frost that never thaws on mountain tops
o.o4: Snow that has been pressed into ice

kz-ce7gdf.e: Permafrost holds huge amounts of carbon, which can be released as greenhouse gases when the ground thaws.

kz-7z1lyk.p: True or false: Sea levels rise when icebergs floating in the sea melt.
kz-7z1lyk.e: Floating ice already displaces its own weight in water. It is ice on land – glaciers and the ice sheet – that makes the sea rise.

kz-shgii8.p: True or false: Most of the oxygen we breathe comes from rainforests.
kz-shgii8.e: At least half of the oxygen is produced by marine phytoplankton. The rainforest itself uses almost all the oxygen it produces.

kz-1iortjx.p: What is the world's tallest animal?
kz-1iortjx.e: An adult male giraffe can grow up to six metres tall. The tongue alone is half a metre long.

kz-j1kslg.p: Which animal has the highest blood pressure?
kz-j1kslg.e: The heart has to pump blood two metres vertically up to the brain. The blood pressure is roughly twice as high as a human's.

kz-zn4eht.p: What does a panda eat almost exclusively?
kz-zn4eht.e: A panda spends up to 14 hours a day eating 12–38 kilograms of bamboo. Its digestive system is still that of a carnivore.

kz-153yt4t.p: What colour is a hippo's sweat?
kz-153yt4t.e: The skin secretes a red fluid that acts like sunscreen and inhibits bacteria. In the old days people believed hippos sweated blood.

kz-18c5he7.p: Which animal kills the most people each year?
kz-18c5he7.e: Mosquitoes spread malaria, dengue fever and other diseases that cost several hundred thousand lives every year. Sharks kill about ten.

kz-16aa19c.p: How many stomachs does a cow have?
kz-16aa19c.e: The rumen, reticulum, omasum and abomasum are compartments of the same stomach. Food is regurgitated and chewed once more along the way.

kz-1g5ravw.p: What is a polar bear's fur really like?
kz-1g5ravw.e: The hairs are hollow and have no colour. They look white because they scatter light – just like snow.

kz-1t82xl2.p: Which animal has the largest eyes in the animal kingdom?
kz-1t82xl2.e: The eyes can reach 27 centimetres in diameter – the size of a football.

kz-1sf083d.p: What is special about the reproduction of the seahorse?

o.o1: The male carries and gives birth to the young
o.o2: The female lays eggs on land
o.o3: The young are born with lungs
o.o4: The eggs hatch only after several years

kz-1sf083d.e: The female deposits the eggs in the male's brood pouch, and he gives birth to up to several hundred young after a couple of weeks.

kz-qf03ke.p: True or false: An ostrich sticks its head in the sand when it is frightened.
kz-qf03ke.e: The ostrich lies flat with its neck along the ground – or runs at up to 70 kilometres an hour.

kz-1cayefr.p: True or false: Goldfish have a memory span of three seconds.
kz-1cayefr.e: Goldfish can remember for months and can be trained, among other things, to recognise colours and find their way through a maze.

kz-cl39zy.p: True or false: Bulls become enraged by the colour red.
kz-cl39zy.e: Cattle cannot distinguish red from green. It is the bullfighter's movements with the cape that make the bull attack.

kz-9olh7s.p: Which of these animals is not a reptile?
kz-9olh7s.e: The salamander is an amphibian, like frogs and toads. It has moist skin without scales.

kz-1f3hji6.p: Which of these animals is not a fish?
kz-1f3hji6.e: The sea cow is a mammal that breathes with lungs. Rays, eels and seahorses are all fish.

kz-15vguby.p: Which predator returned to Denmark in 2012 after 199 years' absence?
kz-15vguby.e: A wolf was found dead in Thy in 2012. In 2017 a pair of wolves produced the first Danish pups in over 200 years.

kz-16r33tj.p: What is Denmark's largest land predator?
kz-16r33tj.e: Until the wolf returned, the title belonged to the badger.

kz-ohfh5y.p: What is Denmark's only venomous snake?
kz-ohfh5y.e: The adder can be recognised by the zigzag stripe down its back. The slow worm is not a snake at all, but a legless lizard.

kz-1k6ly7v.e: The goldcrest weighs only five to six grams – about as much as a sheet of A4 paper.

kz-9jcf3q.p: Which large animal was released on Bornholm in 2012?
kz-9jcf3q.e: The bison in Almindingen were meant to keep the forest open. The species had been completely wiped out in the wild in the 1920s.

kz-1daup5v.p: What is the name of the small whale common in Danish waters?
kz-1daup5v.e: The harbour porpoise is only about one and a half metres long. Its Danish name literally means “sea pig” and has nothing to do with the pet guinea pig.

o.o1: Huge flocks of starlings over the marshes
o.o2: A total solar eclipse in the Nordic region
o.o3: Midwinter north of the Arctic Circle

kz-1rz2pzk.e: In spring and autumn, up to a million starlings gather at Tønder Marsh and form undulating patterns in the evening sky.

kz-hliz5p.p: Which Nordic animal is the only deer where the females also have antlers?
kz-hliz5p.e: Females keep their antlers all winter, while the males shed theirs in December – so Santa's reindeer must be females.

kz-15w8v4x.p: Which bird, which among other places nests on Møns Klint, is the fastest animal in the world?
kz-15w8v4x.e: The peregrine falcon can reach over 300 kilometres per hour when it dives on its prey.

kz-iqsipp.e: The tusk is a left canine tooth that grows up to three metres out through the upper lip. In the Middle Ages it was sold as unicorn horn.

kz-ef43qv.p: True or false: There are penguins in Greenland.
kz-ef43qv.e: Penguins live only in the southern hemisphere. The North Atlantic great auk, which looked like them, was wiped out in 1844.

kz-11stif6.p: True or false: Wild elk have lived in Denmark in recent times.
kz-11stif6.e: Elk occasionally swim across the Øresund from Sweden, and in 2015 elk were released in Lille Vildmose.

kz-155igbw.p: What is the light phenomenon that dances across the night sky over the Nordkalotten called?
kz-155igbw.e: Northern lights occur when charged particles from the Sun hit the atmosphere. Green light comes from oxygen, and red and violet from nitrogen.

kz-w6tw9g.p: What is the highest mountain in Scandinavia?
kz-w6tw9g.e: Galdhøpiggen in Norway is 2,469 metres. Kebnekaise is Sweden's highest and Hvannadalshnúkur is Iceland's.

kz-njrpdu.p: What is the largest lake in the Nordic region?
kz-njrpdu.e: Vänern in Sweden is Europe's third-largest lake and ten times as big as Bornholm.

kz-1vbhb0q.p: Which national park became Denmark's first in 2008?
kz-1vbhb0q.e: Thy was the first. The Wadden Sea is the largest and was also added to UNESCO's World Heritage list in 2014.

o.o1: A wandering dune that moves every year
o.o2: An old milestone on the Hærvejen
o.o3: A kilometre-long beach ridge of flint
o.o4: A raised bog with rare orchids

kz-161ky4y.e: The dune near Skagen moves about 15 metres north-east each year. The buried church nearby shows what the sand can do.

kz-5ueorq.p: Why is it light all night north of the Arctic Circle in summer?

o.o1: The Earth's axis tilts towards the Sun
o.o2: The Earth is closest to the Sun
o.o4: The atmosphere is thinner in the north

kz-5ueorq.e: In summer the North Pole faces the Sun, so it never sets. In winter it is the opposite – the polar night.

o.o1: Light from plankton in the sea

kz-4fs0kf.e: Tiny algae emit a blue-green light when the water is disturbed. It is best seen on still, dark late-summer nights.

kz-f8sitp.p: What created most of Denmark's hills, valleys and fjords?
kz-f8sitp.e: The ice pushed soil and stone ahead of it and left the landscape behind when it melted more than ten thousand years ago.

kz-12gozpi.p: What is the name of the volcano that paralysed European air traffic in 2010?
kz-12gozpi.e: The ash cloud cancelled more than 100,000 flights in a week – and gave news presenters around the world sweaty brows.

kz-1voe82b.p: Which tree can live the longest in Denmark?
kz-1voe82b.e: The King's Oak in Jægerspris Nordskov is estimated to be between 1,500 and 2,000 years old and may be Northern Europe's oldest living tree.

o.o1: A hot spring that spouts water up
o.o2: A crack where lava flows out
o.o3: A lake in an old volcanic crater

kz-ch0wwf.e: The word comes from the Icelandic spring Geysir. The neighbouring Strokkur erupts every five to ten minutes.

kz-47krvf.p: True or false: Heather on the Jutland heaths is a natural landscape that has always been there.
kz-47krvf.e: The heath arose when Stone Age farmers cleared the forest. Without grazing or burning, it turns back into forest.

kz-1sh67jy.p: True or false: Iceland lies on top of a rift between two continental plates.
kz-1sh67jy.e: The Mid-Atlantic Ridge runs straight through the country, which grows a few centimetres wider every year.

kz-1ucga6g.p: What did the Wright brothers invent in 1903?
kz-1ucga6g.e: The first flight lasted 12 seconds and covered 37 metres – shorter than the wingspan of a jumbo jet.

kz-efhts1.p: What did Alexander Fleming discover by chance in 1928?
kz-efhts1.e: A mould had killed the bacteria in a dish he had forgotten before the summer holiday.

kz-440ikd.p: What was the glue on Post-it notes originally?
kz-440ikd.e: In 1968 the chemist Spencer Silver developed a glue that barely stuck. It was only years later that a colleague used it for bookmarks in his hymnbook.

kz-157cce4.p: Which carpenter from Billund founded LEGO in 1932?
kz-157cce4.e: The name is a contraction of “leg godt” (“play well”). The brick with tubes inside was patented by his son Godtfred in 1958.

kz-fls61l.p: What did Valdemar Poulsen invent in 1898?

o.o4: A ballpoint pen with an ink cartridge

kz-fls61l.e: The telegraphone was the first machine that could record sound magnetically – the forerunner of the tape recorder and the hard drive.

kz-67xchq.p: What did Peter L. Jensen from Falster invent in California in 1915?
kz-67xchq.e: The company Magnavox – Latin for great voice – had its breakthrough when President Wilson spoke through the loudspeakers in 1919.

kz-1oy0ry2.p: Which invention from 1867 made Alfred Nobel rich?
kz-1oy0ry2.e: A French newspaper mistakenly printed his obituary under the headline “The merchant of death is dead”. This is said to have led him to establish the Nobel Prize.

kz-1m9rc1m.p: What was the microwave oven discovered by accident using?

o.o1: A chocolate bar melting in a pocket
o.o3: A cup of coffee that stayed warm

kz-1m9rc1m.e: The engineer Percy Spencer was working with radar in 1945 when he noticed his candy bar melting. He then tried popcorn.

kz-1rjctmk.p: What was the first item with a barcode to be scanned in a shop?
kz-1rjctmk.e: It happened in Ohio in 1974. The pack of Wrigley's Juicy Fruit is today in a museum.

kz-gvef9r.p: Which material did Stephanie Kwolek invent in 1965?
kz-gvef9r.e: The fibre is five times stronger than steel by weight and is used in bulletproof vests.

kz-142yk4r.p: What inspired the inventor of Velcro?

o.o1: Burrs stuck in a dog's fur
o.o2: A gecko's feet on a glass window
o.o3: A spider's web in a bush

kz-142yk4r.e: The Swiss George de Mestral saw under a microscope that the burrs had tiny hooks. The name is a blend of “velours” and “crochet”.

kz-1q2jmqy.p: Which of these aids is the oldest?
kz-1q2jmqy.e: Spectacles were made in Italy at the end of the 1200s. The other three came about around the year 1600.

kz-15xfkqz.p: True or false: The tin can was invented several decades before the tin opener.
kz-15xfkqz.e: The can came in 1810, the tin opener only in the 1850s. Until then, the tins said that they should be opened with a hammer and chisel.

kz-1o74r66.p: True or false: Chewing gum was sold in shops before toothpaste came in tubes.
kz-1o74r66.e: The first chewing gum went on sale in the USA in 1848. Toothpaste in tubes was only sold from the 1890s.

kz-rlg2p7.p: Which country switched from left-hand to right-hand traffic during the night of 3 September 1967?
kz-rlg2p7.e: H-Day – “högertrafik”, right-hand traffic – required 360,000 road signs to be changed. Iceland followed the year after.

kz-1i8drf8.p: Which car was the first to be mass-produced on an assembly line?
kz-1i8drf8.e: From 1913 a car could be assembled in an hour and a half. The price fell to under a third.

kz-t0rtqh.e: The brand was founded in 1937 to build a car that ordinary Germans could afford.

kz-1nwwr2e.p: Which railway route is the longest in the world?
kz-1nwwr2e.e: The journey from Moscow to Vladivostok is 9,289 kilometres and takes six days through eight time zones.

kz-1t4ngdd.p: Which Danish ferry route was the country’s most important until the bridge opened in 1998?
kz-1t4ngdd.e: The Great Belt ferries sailed for more than a hundred years. The crossing took an hour – the bridge does it in ten minutes.

kz-ti87si.p: Which supersonic aircraft carried passengers between Europe and New York from 1976 to 2003?
kz-ti87si.e: The journey took under three and a half hours at twice the speed of sound. The Soviet Tu-144 only flew scheduled services briefly.

kz-7vtlkz.p: What does a yellow background on a Danish number plate show?

o.o1: The car is a commercial van

kz-7vtlkz.e: Yellow plates are fitted to commercial vehicles such as vans.

kz-odzp74.p: True or false: The first electric cars were on the roads before the petrol car became widespread.
kz-odzp74.e: Around 1900 a third of the cars in the USA were electric. Cheap petrol and the electric starter later gave the petrol car the upper hand.

kz-1ykg8xm.p: True or false: A passenger plane can keep flying and land on just one engine.
kz-1ykg8xm.e: Twin-engined aircraft are built and certified to fly for hours on one engine. That is why they are allowed to cross oceans.

kz-cq9l7j.p: What does it mean when a product is marked “best before”?

o.o1: The quality may decline after the date
o.o2: The product is dangerous after the date
o.o3: The product must not be sold after the date
o.o4: The product must be kept chilled after the date

kz-cq9l7j.e: “Best before” is about quality – look, smell and taste. It is the “use by” date that you should take seriously.

kz-188cy77.p: Which number do you call to reach the out-of-hours GP service in Region Hovedstaden?
kz-188cy77.e: 112 is the emergency number, and 114 is the police service number. 1813 is also the year of the state bankruptcy.

kz-flvs46.p: What happens to the boiling point of water when you are high up in the mountains?
kz-flvs46.e: On the top of Mount Everest water boils at about 70 degrees, because the air pressure is low. That makes it hard to boil an egg.

kz-1bbioy3.p: Why do most zips have the letters YKK on the pull?

o.o1: It is the name of the manufacturer
o.o2: It is a standard for tooth size
o.o3: It shows that the zip is stainless

kz-1bbioy3.e: Japan's Yoshida Kōgyō Kabushikigaisha makes about half of the world's zips.

kz-iri51c.p: What is the small hole in the side of the cap of a ballpoint pen for?

o.o1: So you can get air if it is swallowed
o.o2: So the ink does not dry out
o.o3: So the cap sits more firmly
o.o4: So the pressure equalises in your pocket

kz-iri51c.e: BIC introduced the hole in 1991 as a safety measure against choking.

kz-1serx2k.p: What do the numbers 0, 1, 2 and 3 stamped on a Danish egg first show?
kz-1serx2k.e: 0 is organic, 1 free-range, 2 barn and 3 cage.

kz-r37ks7.p: Why are there small bumps on the F and J keys of a keyboard?

o.o1: So you can find the keys without looking
o.o2: So the keys wear down less
o.o4: So blind people can read the letters

kz-r37ks7.e: The index fingers rest on F and J in the touch-typing system. From there the rest of the keys can be reached without looking.

kz-a2ud50.p: What do the surfactants in washing-up liquid do to water?

o.o4: Bind the limescale in the water

kz-a2ud50.e: With lower surface tension, the water can creep under the grease and lift it off.

kz-5lswwa.p: How many A4 sheets fit on an A0 sheet?
kz-5lswwa.e: Each step halves the sheet: A0 is exactly one square metre, and an A4 sheet is one sixteenth of it.

kz-tcrbmo.p: What does the drying symbol on a care label mean, showing a square with a circle inside?

o.o2: Should be hung up to dry

kz-tcrbmo.e: Dots in the circle indicate the heat. If the symbol is crossed out, the garment must not go in the tumble dryer.

kz-pxacc5.p: True or false: Getting cold makes you catch a cold.
kz-pxacc5.e: Colds are caused by viruses. We are more often ill in winter, partly because we spend more time close together indoors.

kz-1h6f3g7.p: True or false: Switching off the light wastes electricity if you will be back in a few minutes.
kz-1h6f3g7.e: Modern bulbs do not use extra power to switch back on. It always pays to switch off.

kz-1ndrgcp.p: True or false: Sugar makes children hyperactive.
kz-1ndrgcp.e: Experiments in which nobody knew the children’s diet show no difference – parents’ expectations play a big part.

kz-1gdxo6x.e: The horizontal, oblong pupils give goats and sheep a field of view of almost 340 degrees, so they can spot predators.

kz-ay8472.p: Which country has more sheep than people – about five per inhabitant?
kz-ay8472.e: In the 1980s there were 22 sheep per New Zealander. Today the number has fallen to around five.

kz-sklqkg.p: How does the Eiffel Tower in summer compare with winter?
kz-sklqkg.e: The iron expands in the heat. The sun can also make the top lean a few centimetres away from the warm side.

kz-720uyv.p: Where is the world's shortest scheduled flight, which lasts under two minutes?
kz-720uyv.e: The route between Westray and Papa Westray is 2.7 kilometres. With a tailwind the record is 53 seconds.

kz-1x53trs.p: True or false: Hippo milk is pink.
kz-1x53trs.e: It is a persistent internet myth – the milk is white. The story comes from the reddish secretion the hippo gives off through its skin.

kz-tk389u.p: What is the maximum number of times you can fold an ordinary sheet of paper in half?
kz-tk389u.e: The thickness doubles with each fold. The record of 12 was set with a toilet roll more than a kilometre long.

kz-1n35bcz.p: What was ketchup sold as in the USA of the 1830s?
kz-1n35bcz.e: A doctor in Ohio marketed tomato ketchup as a remedy for indigestion – also in pill form.

kz-ua8a2o.p: What is the fear called that a duck is watching you?
kz-ua8a2o.e: The word was coined by the cartoonist Gary Larson in the strip The Far Side – so it is a joke, not a diagnosis.

kz-1mm4zdu.p: True or false: Honey found in Egyptian tombs is still edible.
kz-1mm4zdu.e: Honey contains so little water and so much sugar that bacteria cannot live in it.

kz-1clq0w7.p: True or false: There are more trees on Earth than stars in the Milky Way.
kz-1clq0w7.e: Earth has around three trillion trees. The Milky Way has 100–400 billion stars.

kz-1b3o9si.p: True or false: The unicorn is Scotland's national animal.
kz-1b3o9si.e: The unicorn has been used in the Scottish royal coat of arms since the 1100s as a symbol of purity and strength.

kz-1g8l9i2.p: True or false: A cloud can weigh several hundred tonnes.
kz-1g8l9i2.e: An ordinary cumulus cloud holds around 500 tonnes of water – spread across droplets so small that the air can carry them.

kz-vg78ip.p: How many Oscars did Titanic win – a record it shares with two other films?
kz-vg78ip.e: “Ben-Hur”, “Titanic” and “The Lord of the Rings: The Return of the King” have all won 11 statuettes.

kz-1udbp9v.p: Which film became the first non-English-language winner of the Oscar for Best Picture in 2020?
kz-1udbp9v.e: Bong Joon-ho's South Korean satire also won the Palme d'Or in Cannes.

kz-yylfgd.e: The film won the Palme d'Or in 1994 and made non-chronological storytelling fashionable.

kz-sc77lw.e: The newspaper magnate's last word turns out to be the name of his childhood sledge – a symbol of everything money could not buy.

kz-1poxpzk.p: In which film does the computer HAL 9000 refuse to open a hatch for the astronaut Dave?
kz-1poxpzk.e: Stanley Kubrick's film from 1968 was made the year before a man landed on the Moon.

kz-17w4z39.p: Which director is behind Spirited Away and My Neighbour Totoro?
kz-17w4z39.e: Miyazaki is a co-founder of Studio Ghibli. Spirited Away won an Oscar in 2003.

kz-d9n7tz.p: Who played the Joker in The Dark Knight?
kz-d9n7tz.e: Ledger died before the premiere and was awarded an Oscar posthumously.

kz-ifaibz.p: Which silent film star hangs from a clock high above the street in Safety Last! from 1923?
kz-ifaibz.e: Lloyd did the stunt himself – with only eight fingers after a prop bomb had cost him two.

kz-23q7d1.p: Which film movement does Bicycle Thieves from 1948 belong to?
kz-23q7d1.e: The neorealists filmed in the streets with non-professional actors and portrayed everyday life in post-war Italy.

kz-1ef5vd9.p: Which film ends with the words about “the beginning of a beautiful friendship”?
kz-1ef5vd9.e: Humphrey Bogart's Rick speaks the line to police chief Renault as they walk off into the fog.

kz-keq1v6.p: Who composed the music for Star Wars, Jaws and Indiana Jones?
kz-keq1v6.e: Williams has been nominated for over 50 Oscars – more than any other living person.

kz-egq4sc.p: Who composed the music for The Good, the Bad and the Ugly?
kz-egq4sc.e: Morricone used whistling, whip cracks and howls and redefined the sound of the western.

kz-ulmagg.p: Who has played James Bond in the most films in the official series?
kz-ulmagg.e: Moore made seven films. Connery made six – plus one outside the series.

kz-8bdn85.p: What does the Bechdel test require of a film?

o.o1: That two women talk about something other than a man
o.o2: That half the roles are women
o.o3: That the director is a woman
o.o4: That the main character is a woman

kz-8bdn85.e: The test comes from a 1985 comic strip by Alison Bechdel. Surprisingly many blockbusters fail it.

kz-1opbdck.p: True or false: Darth Vader says “Luke, I am your father” in The Empire Strikes Back.
kz-1opbdck.e: The line is “No, I am your father”. The wrong version is one of film history's most widespread misquotations.

kz-1wtw0gk.e: The Godfather is from 1972, Jaws from 1975, Star Wars from 1977 and Alien from 1979.

kz-1j5bsx.p: Put Christopher Nolan's films in order by premiere.
kz-1j5bsx.e: Memento came out in 2000, The Dark Knight in 2008, Inception in 2010 and Oppenheimer in 2023.

kz-1yj0gze.p: Which film gave Denmark its first Oscar for Best Foreign Language Film in 1988?
kz-1yj0gze.e: Gabriel Axel's film is based on a novella by Karen Blixen. The following year “Pelle the Conqueror” was the winner.

kz-t4l7mk.p: How many Danish films have won the Oscar for Best International Feature Film?
kz-t4l7mk.e: “Babette's Feast”, “Pelle the Conqueror”, “In a Better World” and “Another Round”.

kz-nmfdei.p: What does Egon Olsen always say when he comes out of Vridsløse?

kz-1tu285d.p: Which safe brand is Egon Olsen's speciality?
kz-1tu285d.e: Egon opens the safes with a stethoscope and a fingertip sense. The company is fictitious.

kz-o82hv0.p: What did the Dogme 95 rules forbid?
kz-o82hv0.e: The rules required precisely a handheld camera, colour and shooting on location. Sound and picture had to be recorded together.

kz-1ugcq33.p: Which blood alcohol level do the teachers try to keep in Another Round?
kz-1ugcq33.e: The theory that people are born with half a per mille too little alcohol in their blood is attributed to the Norwegian psychiatrist Finn Skårderud.

kz-iqret.p: Which actor has the lead role in both The Hunt and Another Round?
kz-iqret.e: Both films are directed by Thomas Vinterberg. The Hunt won Mikkelsen the prize for best actor in Cannes.

kz-1hsdedm.p: Which comedy from 2000 is about four small-time criminals who open a restaurant in a forest?
kz-1hsdedm.e: Anders Thomas Jensen's first feature film became a cult classic with Søren Pilmark, Ulrich Thomsen, Mads Mikkelsen and Nikolaj Lie Kaas.

kz-116z6t.p: Who directed the silent film The Passion of Joan of Arc from 1928?
kz-116z6t.e: The film consists almost entirely of close-ups and is regarded as one of the masterpieces of film history.

kz-9ktajc.p: Which film company with a polar bear on a globe is one of the world's oldest still making films?
kz-9ktajc.e: The company was founded in Valby in 1906 by Ole Olsen.

kz-1bymnxw.p: What was the name of the comedy duo that were Denmark's first international film stars in the 1920s?
kz-1bymnxw.e: The tall Carl Schenstrøm and the small Harald Madsen were the model for many later comedy duos.

kz-17xfr9c.p: Which Danish actress was the silent film's first great European star?
kz-17xfr9c.e: In Germany she was simply called “Die Asta”. Her breakthrough came with Afgrunden in 1910.

kz-14hgjlq.p: What is the name of the film prize that Danish film critics have awarded since 1948?
kz-14hgjlq.e: It is named after the actresses Bodil Ipsen and Bodil Kjer. The Robert Prize is awarded by the Danish Film Academy.

kz-6ndm3j.p: Which animated film from 1986 is based on Peter Madsen's comic strip about the Nordic gods?
kz-6ndm3j.e: The film was at the time the most expensive Danish film ever made.

kz-lvcqe3.p: Who voices almost all the characters in Terkel in Trouble?
kz-lvcqe3.e: The story began as a radio serial for children.

kz-1imlvfp.p: Which film from 2012 is about Struensee, Christian VII and Queen Caroline Mathilde?
kz-1imlvfp.e: The film was nominated for an Oscar and starred Mads Mikkelsen and Alicia Vikander.

kz-1clyrf2.p: Which film from 2015 is about German prisoners of war clearing mines on the west coast?
kz-1clyrf2.e: Around two million land mines lay along the Danish west coast after the war. About half of the mine clearers were killed or wounded.

kz-1w9d8ny.p: What do the two butchers in The Green Butchers sell with great success?
kz-1w9d8ny.e: The meat is sold as “chicken fillings”. Mads Mikkelsen and Nikolaj Lie Kaas play the butchers.

kz-1b1mlkf.p: Put the films in order by premiere.
kz-1b1mlkf.e: Pelle the Conqueror is from 1987, The Celebration (Festen) from 1998, Adam's Apples from 2005 and Another Round from 2020.

kz-1on81i8.p: True or false: The Celebration (Festen) was the very first Dogme film.
kz-1on81i8.e: Thomas Vinterberg's film received Dogme certificate number 1 and won the Jury Prize in Cannes in 1998.

kz-1ymsf4p.p: In which city is Breaking Bad set?
kz-1ymsf4p.e: The series was supposed to be filmed in California, but New Mexico offered a better tax arrangement.

kz-1x4ydur.p: What does Walter White teach before he becomes a drug kingpin?
kz-1x4ydur.e: His alias Heisenberg is borrowed from the German quantum physicist.

kz-1gx7wng.p: What is the café called in Friends?
kz-1gx7wng.e: MacLaren's is the pub in How I Met Your Mother, and Monk's is the diner in Seinfeld.

kz-efjxgl.p: How many seasons did Friends have?
kz-efjxgl.e: The final episode in 2004 was watched by over 52 million Americans.

kz-7onvhd.p: Which Danish actor plays Jaime Lannister in Game of Thrones?
kz-7onvhd.e: Pilou Asbæk is also in it – as the pirate king Euron Greyjoy.

kz-11vur22.p: Which series has a dark parallel world called The Upside Down?
kz-11vur22.e: The series is set in the 1980s in the fictional town of Hawkins, Indiana.

kz-o91xsi.p: What does Don Draper do for a living in Mad Men?
kz-o91xsi.e: The title refers to Madison Avenue in New York, where the big advertising agencies were based.

kz-xdkkno.p: What is the paper company called in the American version of The Office?
kz-xdkkno.e: Wernham Hogg is the company in the British original with Ricky Gervais.

kz-ybiuvo.p: Who plays Queen Elizabeth in the first two seasons of The Crown?
kz-ybiuvo.e: The role changed actor every other season: first Foy, then Colman and finally Staunton.

kz-kjnwle.p: Which children's game opens the contest in Squid Game?
kz-kjnwle.e: The series from 2021 became one of Netflix's biggest hits ever.

kz-1bsmyph.p: Which series from 1990 is about the question: Who killed Laura Palmer?
kz-1bsmyph.e: David Lynch's series mixed crime drama, soap opera and nightmare in a way television had never seen before.

kz-6rmd5c.p: At which hospital do the doctors work in the first seasons of Grey's Anatomy?
kz-6rmd5c.e: County General is the hospital in ER, Princeton-Plainsboro in House and Sacred Heart in Scrubs.

kz-1k1wjmz.p: What does the time machine in Doctor Who look like from the outside?
kz-1k1wjmz.e: The TARDIS is bigger on the inside than the outside. The series has been running since 1963.

kz-q1dos2.p: Which animated series has been running continuously on American television since 1989?
kz-q1dos2.e: No other American primetime fiction series has had more episodes.

kz-1yn6ob6.p: Which HBO series is about the Roy family and their media company?
kz-1yn6ob6.e: Creator Jesse Armstrong has said that the family is partly inspired by the media mogul Rupert Murdoch.

kz-atkpeq.p: Which series has the episodes “San Junipero” and “Nosedive”?
kz-atkpeq.e: The title refers to the black, blank screen of a switched-off phone.

kz-1mdorwr.p: Which British series follows the aristocratic Crawley family and their servants?
kz-1mdorwr.e: The series begins with the sinking of the Titanic in 1912 and is filmed at Highclere Castle.

kz-9zj6ev.p: In which city is The Wire set?
kz-9zj6ev.e: Creator David Simon was a crime reporter at the city's newspaper for 13 years.

kz-1e2n3gv.p: Which series begins with Oceanic Flight 815 crashing on a deserted island?
kz-1e2n3gv.e: The 2004 pilot episode was the most expensive in ABC’s history.

kz-eobrqa.p: What is the name of Tony Soprano's psychiatrist?
kz-eobrqa.e: The conversations with Dr Melfi are the backbone of the series, which is often ranked as the best ever.

kz-wjupp1.p: True or false: The actors in Friends all received the same salary in the final seasons.
kz-wjupp1.e: They negotiated together and eventually got a million dollars per episode each.

kz-5lyi0x.p: What is the name of the bank that Mads Skjern opens in Matador?
kz-5lyi0x.e: Korsbæk Bank is the old bank, which Hans Christian Varnæs runs.

kz-s2x1lf.p: How many episodes does Matador have?
kz-s2x1lf.e: The series was first broadcast from 1978 to 1982 and has been repeated again and again.

kz-110gfi5.e: From the Wall Street crash, through the occupation, to the first years after the war.

kz-19q5366.p: Who plays Mads Skjern in Matador?
kz-19q5366.e: Holger Juul Hansen plays bank director Varnæs, Buster Larsen the pig dealer and Ove Sprogøe Doctor Hansen.

kz-hbcnwm.p: Who plays Prime Minister Birgitte Nyborg in Borgen?
kz-hbcnwm.e: Birgitte Hjort Sørensen plays the journalist Katrine Fønsmark.

kz-snl47m.p: What is the name of Birgitte Nyborg's spin doctor in Borgen?
kz-snl47m.e: Kasper Juul is played by Pilou Asbæk.

kz-4r262k.p: What became Sarah Lund's trademark in The Killing?
kz-4r262k.e: The sweater from Gudrun & Gudrun sold out across Europe when the series was shown on the BBC.

kz-11zlsfv.p: What is Frank's girlfriend called in Klown?
kz-11zlsfv.e: Iben is Casper's girlfriend. The series is inspired by the American “Curb Your Enthusiasm”.

kz-g39f6.p: Which TV series from 1991 is set in December on a Jutland potato farm and mixes Danish and English?
kz-g39f6.e: The three gnomes Hansi, Günther and Fritz were played by De Nattergale, who also wrote the songs.

kz-9mq6g4.p: Which series from 2000 follows a mobile murder squad with Charlotte Fich and Mads Mikkelsen?
kz-9mq6g4.e: The series won an international Emmy in 2002 – the first for a Danish drama series.

kz-pxoav7.p: Which crime series begins with a body lying exactly on the border between Denmark and Sweden?
kz-pxoav7.e: The body turns out to be two halves, one from each country, so Swedish and Danish police must cooperate.

kz-11ef0yh.p: In which year does the action in Seaside Hotel begin?
kz-11ef0yh.e: Each season covers one summer. The last takes place in 1946.

kz-f5ouh3.p: Which series by Adam Price is about a Copenhagen clergy family?
kz-f5ouh3.e: Lars Mikkelsen won an international Emmy for the role of the provost Johannes Krogh.

kz-1ipbbli.p: What animal is Dolph in Dolph & Wulff?
kz-1ipbbli.e: The light-blue hippo comes from the comic strip Wulffmorgenthaler.

kz-18fzdq.p: Who plays Maude Varnæs in Matador?

kz-1nfz7f2.e: The House on Christianshavn began in 1970, A Provincial Town in 1977, Matador in 1978 and The Village in 1991.

kz-qakg42.p: True or false: “Matador” is named after a board game.
kz-qakg42.e: The title refers to the game in which you buy plots and outcompete each other – as Mads Skjern does in Korsbæk.

kz-1ehpwws.p: Which Beatle walks barefoot across the zebra crossing on the cover of Abbey Road?
kz-1ehpwws.e: The bare feet became a central element in the persistent conspiracy theory that Paul had died.

kz-7imz8x.p: Which instrument did Miles Davis play?
kz-7imz8x.e: His 1959 album “Kind of Blue” is one of the best-selling jazz albums in the world.

kz-1ci1aeo.p: How many symphonies did Beethoven write?
kz-1ci1aeo.e: The ninth, with the “Ode to Joy”, premiered in 1824, when he was almost completely deaf.

kz-1xuewco.e: The four violin concertos from 1725 were accompanied by poems describing everything from birdsong to chattering teeth.

kz-11tfr4g.p: How many lines does a staff have?
kz-11tfr4g.e: The notes' positions on and between the five lines show the pitch.

kz-8g8y6a.p: What does it mean when a choir sings a cappella?
kz-8g8y6a.e: The term means “as in the chapel” – that is, like church singing without accompaniment.

kz-288uzu.p: Which song did ABBA win Eurovision with in 1974?
kz-288uzu.e: The United Kingdom gave the song zero points. It has since been named the best Eurovision entry ever.

kz-1186q72.p: Which singer was born Farrokh Bulsara?
kz-1186q72.e: Queen's frontman was born on Zanzibar in 1946 and partly grew up in India.

kz-13a3nbm.p: Who is the only artist to have won the Grammy for Album of the Year four times?
kz-13a3nbm.e: She won for “Fearless”, “1989”, “Folklore” and “Midnights”. Wonder, Sinatra and Paul Simon have three each.

kz-1nm2yjy.p: Which band released The Dark Side of the Moon?
kz-1nm2yjy.e: The album from 1973 was on the American chart for over 900 weeks.

kz-a59dl7.p: Which festival in 1969 became the high point of the hippie era?
kz-a59dl7.e: The organisers expected 50,000 guests. Around 400,000 came to a field in New York State.

kz-1qjnjui.p: Which of these musicians did not die at the age of 27?
kz-1qjnjui.e: Elvis died at 42. Hendrix, Joplin and Cobain belong with Jim Morrison and Amy Winehouse in the “27 Club”.

kz-ywq5m5.p: Which opera ends with the geisha Cio-Cio-San taking her own life?
kz-ywq5m5.e: All four operas were written by Puccini. The premiere of Madama Butterfly in 1904 was a failure.

kz-1w8kp8.e: The opera premiered in Vienna two months before Mozart's death in 1791.

kz-1scz4em.p: Which music genre emerged from block parties in the Bronx in the 1970s?
kz-1scz4em.e: DJ Kool Herc extended the drum break by switching between two identical records – and the foundation was laid.

kz-mb56xc.p: Which group did Beyoncé sing in before going solo?
kz-mb56xc.e: The group from Houston had hits with songs including “Say My Name” and “Survivor”.

kz-dfetyi.e: Antonio Stradivari built his instruments in Cremona around the year 1700. The best ones sell for over 100 million kroner.

kz-1l4lkno.p: Which instrument is the symphony orchestra tuned to?
kz-1l4lkno.e: The oboe's tone is penetrating and stable. It plays an A, which the rest of the orchestra tunes to.

kz-2zxvs2.p: True or false: Mozart composed the melody for “Twinkle, Twinkle, Little Star”.
kz-2zxvs2.e: The melody is a French folk song. Mozart wrote twelve variations on it, and that has earned him the credit.

kz-14xfp56.p: Put the artists in order by their record debut – oldest first.
kz-14xfp56.e: Elvis debuted in 1954, The Beatles in 1962, Madonna in 1982 and Adele in 2008.

kz-124vmjw.p: What was the name of Kim Larsen's band from 1995 until his death?
kz-124vmjw.e: With Kjukken, Kim Larsen toured right up until his death in 2018.

kz-1kuc45c.p: Which 1984 film has the songs “Papirsklip” and “Susan Himmelblå”?
kz-1kuc45c.e: Kim Larsen played the lead role himself. The soundtrack album is the best-selling album in Denmark.

kz-1s86qe8.p: What is the name of Roskilde Festival's main stage?
kz-1s86qe8.e: The orange tent was bought second-hand in 1978 – it had toured with The Rolling Stones.

kz-1caf4kn.p: Which song won Denmark Eurovision in 2013?
kz-1caf4kn.e: Emmelie de Forest sang barefoot and won in Malmö.

kz-plssdl.p: Who won Eurovision for Denmark in 1963 with “Dansevise”?
kz-plssdl.e: It was the first time a duo had won the contest.

kz-1fb08as.p: Who composed the opera “Maskarade” and six symphonies?
kz-1fb08as.e: Carl Nielsen grew up in a poor home on Funen and also wrote melodies for many of the best-known songs in the Folk High School Songbook.

o.o1: Kong Christian stod ved højen mast
o.o4: Den danske sang er en ung blond pige

kz-mr9c3a.e: Denmark is one of the few countries with two official national anthems. “Der er et yndigt land” is the civic one.

kz-67gejx.p: Who wrote the lyrics to “Der er et yndigt land”?
kz-67gejx.e: The poem from 1819 has twelve verses. Normally only the first verse and the last lines of the final one are sung.

kz-grqzbs.p: Which Danish singer features on the global hit “Lean On” from 2015?
kz-grqzbs.e: The song with Major Lazer and DJ Snake was for a time the most streamed song ever on Spotify.

kz-1o9uh7x.p: Which Danish band had a global hit with “7 Years”?
kz-1o9uh7x.e: Lead singer Lukas Forchhammer grew up in Christiania. The song was nominated for three Grammys.

kz-1f0ieiu.p: Who was the lead singer of Shu-bi-dua?
kz-1f0ieiu.e: Michael Hardinger was the guitarist and wrote many of the songs together with Bundesen.

kz-gw4fci.p: Which duo is behind the songs “Hot!” and “En dag tilbage”?
kz-gw4fci.e: Niclas Petersen and Jannik Thomsen from Værløse broke through in 2002.

kz-q2ko4w.p: Which Danish group had a hit all over Europe with “Aicha” in 2003?
kz-q2ko4w.e: The three members from Brøndby Strand have roots in Morocco, Pakistan and Honduras.

kz-1pbi59f.p: Which Melodi Grand Prix veteran wrote “Krøller eller ej” and had a son who also became a pop star?
kz-1pbi59f.e: He won the Danish Melodi Grand Prix three times. His son Rasmus broke through in 2009.

kz-yf0qyq.p: Who wrote and sang “Så længe jeg lever” and “Der er noget galt i Danmark”?
kz-yf0qyq.e: John Mogensen died in 1977, only 41 years old, but the songs are still sung.

kz-191ab7n.p: Which songbook from 1894 is Denmark's most widely used for communal singing?
kz-191ab7n.e: The book has appeared in many editions and sold millions of copies.

kz-gtlbfl.p: Which band did Lars Ulrich from Gentofte form in Los Angeles in 1981?
kz-gtlbfl.e: Ulrich was originally a tennis talent and moved to the USA to pursue the sport.

kz-1d2hgoh.p: What is the name of Medina's breakthrough hit from 2008, which later charted in Germany as “You and I”?
kz-1d2hgoh.e: The song became the best-selling single in Denmark in 2009.

kz-mk3673.p: True or false: “Barbie Girl” led the toy company Mattel to sue Aqua's record label.
kz-mk3673.e: The judge dismissed the case and ended by advising the parties to relax.

kz-3bzeg3.e: The novel was published anonymously in 1813. The title page simply said it was written by the author of “Sense and Sensibility”.

kz-kzlhya.e: The novel follows the poor student Raskolnikov, who murders a pawnbroker to prove a theory.

kz-1ml2d99.p: Which animals take power in George Orwell's Animal Farm?
kz-1ml2d99.e: The fable is a satire of the Russian Revolution. The pig Napoleon is Stalin.

kz-kd0wcb.e: The novel from 1925 sold poorly during Fitzgerald's lifetime. He died believing he had been forgotten.

kz-1d4x2sd.p: What is the name of Don Quixote's squire?
kz-1d4x2sd.e: Rocinante is the knight's scrawny horse, and Dulcinea is the peasant girl he has named as his lady.

kz-1emngnr.p: How many years does Odysseus take to get home from Troy?
kz-1emngnr.e: The war itself also lasted ten years, so he was away from Ithaca for twenty.

kz-mr52tz.p: Who guides Dante through Hell in The Divine Comedy?
kz-mr52tz.e: The Roman poet guides him through Hell and Purgatory. In Paradise, Beatrice takes over.

kz-1ci8pwq.e: The Brazilian's novel from 1988 has been translated into over 80 languages.

kz-ib144h.e: Tove Jansson was Finland-Swedish and wrote in Swedish. The first book was published in 1945.

kz-73oxk6.p: What is the name of the hacker in Stieg Larsson's Millennium trilogy?
kz-73oxk6.e: Larsson died in 2004, before the first book was published, and never lived to see its success.

kz-ulq7b3.p: Who wrote The Count of Monte Cristo and The Three Musketeers?
kz-ulq7b3.e: Dumas' grandfather was a French nobleman, and his grandmother was a slave in Haiti.

kz-1jamf8d.p: In which story does Gregor Samsa wake up as a giant insect?
kz-1jamf8d.e: Kafka forbade the insect from being drawn on the cover. The reader was meant to imagine it themselves.

kz-npdvdo.p: Who is the only person to have voluntarily declined the Nobel Prize in Literature?
kz-npdvdo.e: Sartre declined in 1964, because a writer should not allow himself to be turned into an institution.

kz-1gpxwl6.p: Which songwriter won the Nobel Prize in Literature in 2016?
kz-1gpxwl6.e: Dylan did not attend the ceremony and only collected the prize several months later.

kz-1so7moi.p: What is the name of the rootless narrator in The Catcher in the Rye?
kz-1so7moi.e: J.D. Salinger's novel from 1951 has sold over 65 million copies.

kz-1qw8s1d.p: Who wrote To Kill a Mockingbird?
kz-1qw8s1d.e: Truman Capote was Harper Lee's childhood friend and the model for the boy Dill in the novel.

kz-9j554l.p: Which novel opens with the line that all happy families are alike?
kz-9j554l.e: Tolstoy's opening line continues that every unhappy family is unhappy in its own way.

kz-vjqxps.p: Which Irish novel takes place over a single day in Dublin, 16 June 1904?
kz-vjqxps.e: The date is celebrated every year as Bloomsday, after the main character, Leopold Bloom.

kz-3e3d0p.p: True or false: Sherlock Holmes never says “Elementary, my dear Watson” in Conan Doyle's books.
kz-3e3d0p.e: The line comes from later films and stage plays.

kz-1dm7yh0.p: True or false: Frankenstein is the name of the monster in Mary Shelley's novel.
kz-1dm7yh0.e: Victor Frankenstein is the scientist. His creation is never given a name.

kz-xctj87.e: Don Quixote was published in 1605, Robinson Crusoe in 1719, Gulliver's Travels in 1726 and Frankenstein in 1818.

kz-639m56.p: How many Danish authors have won the Nobel Prize in Literature?
kz-639m56.e: Karl Gjellerup and Henrik Pontoppidan shared the prize in 1917, and Johannes V. Jensen won it in 1944.

kz-1kvd6fd.p: What is the name of the Deputy Chief Inspector in Jussi Adler-Olsen's Department Q books?
kz-1kvd6fd.e: Harry Hole and William Wisting are Norwegian, and Wallander is Swedish.

kz-gidqom.p: What is the unwritten law that Aksel Sandemose formulated in 1933 called?
kz-gidqom.e: “You must not think you are anything” is the first of the ten commandments.

kz-2jt7fy.p: Which town was the model for Jante in Sandemose's novel?
kz-2jt7fy.e: Sandemose grew up in the town and wrote the novel “A Fugitive Crosses His Tracks” in Norway.

kz-1y50phe.p: Who wrote about Gummi-Tarzan, Orla Frøsnapper and Lille Virgil?
kz-1y50phe.e: Ole Lund Kirkegaard was a schoolteacher and illustrated his own books.

kz-v42163.p: Who wrote Buster's World and Zappa?
kz-v42163.e: Bjarne Reuter has also written “Drengene fra Sankt Petri” and “Prins Faisals ring”.

kz-avlx36.p: Who drew the pictures for Halfdan's ABC?
kz-avlx36.e: The book came out in 1967 and has become a Danish classic.

kz-4ezh2w.p: Which poet built the long poem “alfabet” on the Fibonacci numbers?
kz-4ezh2w.e: Each section has as many lines as the next number in the sequence. The poem opens with the line “the apricot trees exist”.

kz-1iq6qxy.p: Which young poet sold over 100,000 copies of his debut in 2013?
kz-1iq6qxy.e: The poetry collection, written entirely in capital letters, is the best-selling Danish debut poetry collection ever.

kz-1k5ibss.p: Who wrote the Africa trilogy “Eksil”, “Revolution” and “Liberty”?
kz-1k5ibss.e: Ejersbo died in 2008, aged 40. The trilogy was published after his death.

kz-16ee9ce.p: Who wrote “We, the Drowned” about the seafaring town of Marstal?
kz-16ee9ce.e: The novel from 2006 follows the town's seafarers over a hundred years.

kz-5ppmir.e: Bang was the master of impressionism in Danish prose, and a celebrated reader and stage director.

kz-r2t56n.p: Who wrote “The Neglected Spring”, about the death of a Latin teacher?
kz-r2t56n.e: Teacher Blomme dies from a poisoned malt sweet. The novel is a biting satire of the Danish Latin school.

kz-a5a8j3.p: What is the title of Tom Kristensen's novel about the journalist Ole Jastrau, who drinks himself to ruin?
kz-a5a8j3.e: The novel from 1930 draws on Kristensen's own time as a critic at Politiken.

kz-gvdsso.p: Which hymn writer wrote “Den signede dag” and came up with the idea of the folk high school?
kz-gvdsso.e: Grundtvig wrote several hundred hymns. Nobody has more in the Danish hymnal.

kz-ka5oce.p: Who wrote “Vangede Billeder” and was known as Uncle Danny?
kz-ka5oce.e: “Uncle Danny” wrote around a hundred books before he died in 1993.

kz-1b4zl74.e: “Se, hvilken morgenstund” was sung by Povl Dissing and is one of Denmark's most beloved songs.

kz-1nf0izu.p: What did Piet Hein call his short, pointed poems?
kz-1nf0izu.e: He wrote thousands of them – and also invented the superellipse and the game Hex.

kz-18nzvct.p: True or false: Karen Blixen never won the Nobel Prize in Literature.
kz-18nzvct.e: She was nominated several times. When Hemingway won the prize in 1954, he said it should have gone to her.

kz-17hatu2.e: Holberg's comedy is from 1722, Andersen's fairy tale from 1843, The Fall of the King from 1900 and Childhood Street from 1943.

kz-6ozm88.p: Which museum is the Mona Lisa displayed in?
kz-6ozm88.e: The painting is only 77 by 53 centimetres and hangs behind bulletproof glass.

kz-j2kmg5.p: Which painting was stolen from the Louvre in 1911 and was gone for over two years?
kz-j2kmg5.e: The thief was an Italian craftsman who hid the painting under his coat. The theft is what made the painting world-famous.

kz-g7ev6v.p: Who painted the ceiling of the Sistine Chapel?
kz-g7ev6v.e: The work took four years. Michelangelo regarded himself as a sculptor and took on the task only reluctantly.

kz-zl4a6r.e: There are four versions. One of them sold for almost 120 million dollars in 2012.

kz-phibxh.p: Who painted Girl with a Pearl Earring?
kz-phibxh.e: Only about 35 paintings by Vermeer are known. Nobody knows who the girl was.

kz-egns7j.e: The painting doesn't actually depict a night scene. It only looked dark until old varnish was removed.

kz-1xv53gf.p: Which artist is known for soup cans and brightly coloured Marilyn portraits?
kz-1xv53gf.e: Warhol called his studio “The Factory” and believed everyone would be famous for 15 minutes.

kz-1kky3g5.p: Who exhibited a urinal as an artwork titled “Fountain” in 1917?
kz-1kky3g5.e: The work was rejected by the exhibition, and has since been named the most influential artwork of the 20th century.

kz-1hf47sd.p: Who painted the melting clocks in The Persistence of Memory?
kz-1hf47sd.e: Dalí said the idea came to him when he saw a Camembert melting in the sun.

kz-140oa20.p: Who painted The Kiss with real gold leaf?
kz-140oa20.e: The painting from 1908 hangs in the Belvedere in Vienna and belongs to Klimt's “golden period”.

kz-1dfzom4.p: Which Danish painter is known for quiet, grey interiors with a woman seen from behind?
kz-1dfzom4.e: The woman is usually his wife Ida, and the rooms were at Strandgade 30 on Christianshavn.

kz-1crpwp6.p: Who is called the father of Danish painting?
kz-1crpwp6.e: As a professor at the Royal Danish Academy of Fine Arts, Eckersberg trained a whole generation of Golden Age painters.

kz-fful61.p: Which artists' colony did Anna and Michael Ancher belong to?
kz-fful61.e: Anna Ancher was the only one of the painters who was born in Skagen, at Brøndums Hotel.

kz-13o0inc.p: Which three cities gave their names to the artists' group Cobra?
kz-13o0inc.e: The group was founded in 1948. Asger Jorn was the leading Dane.

kz-z38e9t.p: Which Danish sculptor has his own museum next to Christiansborg?
kz-z38e9t.e: Thorvaldsen lived in Rome for 40 years and was welcomed as a national hero when he returned home in 1838. He is buried in the museum's courtyard.

kz-5qi5x0.p: Who created the sculpture The Little Mermaid at Langelinie?
kz-5qi5x0.e: The brewer Carl Jacobsen commissioned the figure in 1909. She is only 1.25 metres tall.

kz-1wf41u6.p: Which Danish-Icelandic artist created the rainbow walkway on top of ARoS in Aarhus?
kz-1wf41u6.e: “Your Rainbow Panorama” is a 150-metre walk made of coloured glass.

kz-krn5qe.p: What are a painter's three primary colours?
kz-krn5qe.e: Red, green and blue are the primary colours of light, the ones a screen mixes its colours from.

kz-1q0b97h.p: What is it called when you paint directly onto wet lime plaster?
kz-1q0b97h.e: The pigment bonds with the plaster as it dries. The painter therefore has to work quickly and cannot correct the work afterwards.

kz-1ycixab.p: Which street artist had his own painting shredded seconds after it sold at auction in 2018?
kz-1ycixab.e: The shredder was built into the frame. The half-shredded painting was later sold for 18 times as much.

kz-1x5lm1y.p: True or false: Michelangelo lay on his back while painting the ceiling of the Sistine Chapel.
kz-1x5lm1y.e: He stood on a scaffold with his head tilted back, and complained in a poem about what it did to his body.

kz-25jas2.p: True or false: Ancient white marble statues were originally painted in bright colours.
kz-25jas2.e: The colours have worn away over millennia, but traces of pigment show the statues were painted in red, blue and yellow, among other colours.

kz-oqjxsw.e: The Baroque emerged around 1600, Impressionism in the 1870s, Cubism around 1907 and Pop art in the 1950s.

kz-466gyj.p: Which country did Denmark take the Lucia procession tradition from?
kz-466gyj.e: The custom came to Denmark in 1944. Lucia herself was a saint from Sicily.

kz-fadxgi.p: According to legend, which animals gave away Saint Martin when he was hiding?
kz-fadxgi.e: Martin did not want to become a bishop and hid among the geese, which cackled loudly. That is why people eat goose, or duck, on Martinmas Eve.

kz-3hmtft.p: What was originally inside the Shrovetide barrel?
kz-3hmtft.e: The black cat was a symbol of evil, which was to be driven out of the town.

kz-u4rgm4.p: What is the Jewish festival of lights that lasts eight days called?
kz-u4rgm4.e: One more candle is lit each evening on the nine-branched candlestick.

kz-7is5n5.p: How many syllables does a classic haiku have?
kz-7is5n5.e: The syllables are split across three lines of five, seven and five.

kz-106zd1m.p: Which country does the ballet Swan Lake come from?
kz-106zd1m.e: Tchaikovsky's ballet premiered at the Bolshoi Theatre in Moscow in 1877.

kz-1ic15ut.p: Which Danish ballet master created La Sylphide and A Folk Tale?
kz-1ic15ut.e: The Bournonville style is light and airy, and is still danced at the Royal Danish Theatre.

kz-1uea431.p: Which musical is based on T.S. Eliot's poems about cats?
kz-1uea431.e: Andrew Lloyd Webber's musical from 1981 ran for 21 years in London.

kz-1yw1wbz.p: What is the Japanese comic form called that is read from right to left?
kz-1yw1wbz.e: Anime is animation, kabuki is theatre, and origami is paper folding.

kz-ygs4nt.p: How many animals are there in the Chinese zodiac?
kz-ygs4nt.e: Each year has its own animal. According to legend, the rat came first, because it rode on the ox's back.

kz-1ufu45o.p: In which city is the Kaaba, which Muslims face during prayer?
kz-1ufu45o.e: All Muslims who are able to are expected to make a pilgrimage to Mecca once in their lives.

kz-1eyr445.p: What was the name of the founder of Buddhism?
kz-1eyr445.e: He was a prince in what is now Nepal about 2,500 years ago. Buddha means “the awakened one”.

kz-1tkc3bn.p: Which Danish art museum on the Øresund is named after a landowner's three wives?
kz-1tkc3bn.e: The villa's first owner was married three times, and all three wives were called Louise.

kz-18vkx6a.p: Who founded the Ny Carlsberg Glyptotek?
kz-18vkx6a.e: The brewer believed art should be for everyone. His father, J.C. Jacobsen, founded Carlsberg itself.

kz-tfcx7h.p: Which Danish word made the Oxford dictionaries' list of words of the year in 2016?
kz-tfcx7h.e: That year at least nine English books about hygge were published.

kz-1gtv184.p: What is the oldest surviving story in world literature called?
kz-1gtv184.e: The epic about the king of Uruk was written on clay tablets in Mesopotamia over 4,000 years ago.

kz-1ytd9yk.e: The Japanese technique highlights the breaks rather than hiding them.

kz-i9zep2.p: Which city was the home of the ancient Olympic Games?
kz-i9zep2.e: The games were held every four years for over a thousand years in honour of Zeus.

kz-uh0pzr.p: True or false: The fortune cookie with a small note inside comes from China.
kz-uh0pzr.e: It was popularised by Japanese immigrants in California around 1900 and is almost unknown in China.

kz-9meb1e.p: True or false: The Santa Claus we know, in red clothes with a white beard, was invented by Coca-Cola.
kz-9meb1e.e: The red-clad Santa already appeared in drawings from the 1800s. Coca-Cola's adverts from 1931 simply made him even more widespread.

kz-1bffe5y.p: Who designed the chairs known as the Egg, the Swan and the Seven?
kz-1bffe5y.e: The Egg and the Swan were designed for the SAS Royal Hotel in Copenhagen, where Jacobsen decided everything down to the cutlery.

kz-oa9xzc.e: Wegner designed over 500 chairs. One of them became known as “The Chair” when Kennedy and Nixon sat in it during a TV debate.

kz-imeuhn.e: Louis Poulsen is the company that manufactures the lamp. Henningsen was also a revue writer and social critic.

kz-1wj04qk.p: What are the many shades on a PH lamp designed to do?

o.o2: Focus the light into one beam

kz-1wj04qk.e: The shades hide the bulb from every angle and send the light softly downwards.

kz-1i78s7o.p: Who designed the small wooden monkey from 1951?
kz-1i78s7o.e: The monkey is made of teak and limba and consists of 31 parts.

kz-6237vt.p: Who designed the world's first chair moulded in one piece of plastic?
kz-6237vt.e: The S-curved chair from 1960 can be stacked and has neither legs nor joins.

kz-1v7lvmk.p: Which architecture practice is behind the waste incineration plant with a ski slope on Amager?
kz-1v7lvmk.e: Bjarke Ingels Group also designed the 8 House in Ørestad and LEGO House in Billund.

kz-61eqof.p: Which Danish architect designed the Copenhagen Opera House?
kz-61eqof.e: The opera house was a gift from shipowner Mærsk Mc-Kinney Møller, who interfered in many details along the way.

kz-2lzecr.p: Who designed the DR Concert House?
kz-2lzecr.e: The blue cube in Ørestad opened in 2009 and ended up markedly more expensive than planned.

kz-d60gbu.p: What is the Royal Library's extension by Copenhagen harbour called?
kz-d60gbu.e: The façade is clad in polished black granite from Zimbabwe.

kz-1xiy1dg.p: Which king built the Round Tower, Børsen and Rosenborg?
kz-1xiy1dg.e: No Danish king left a bigger mark on Copenhagen. He was king for 60 years (1588–1648).

kz-11t7udy.p: What did the famous spire of Børsen, which collapsed during the fire in 2024, depict?

o.o1: The entwined tails of four dragons

kz-11t7udy.e: According to tradition, the dragons were to protect the building from enemies and fire.

kz-10l1nsj.p: Which architect designed the Guggenheim Museum in Bilbao?
kz-10l1nsj.e: The museum from 1997 turned a worn-out industrial city into a travel destination. The phenomenon is now called the Bilbao effect.

kz-1pq0n3q.p: Which architect is behind the Sagrada Família in Barcelona?
kz-1pq0n3q.e: Gaudí worked on the church for 43 years and is buried in its crypt.

kz-1528w85.p: When did construction of the Sagrada Família begin?
kz-1528w85.e: The church has been under construction for longer than it took to build the pyramids.

kz-1wsdtp9.p: Which school of art and design did Walter Gropius found in 1919?
kz-1wsdtp9.e: The school united art, craft and industry, and was closed by the Nazis in 1933.

kz-atypa7.p: Which architect made the motto “Less is more” famous?
kz-atypa7.e: Mies van der Rohe was the last director of the Bauhaus and later designed glass-and-steel high-rises in the USA.

kz-iz123e.p: Which of the three classical Greek orders of columns is the simplest?
kz-iz123e.e: The Doric column has a smooth, cushion-shaped capital. The Ionic has scrolls, and the Corinthian has acanthus leaves.

kz-1xpbqo7.p: What is the core idea of Copenhagen's 1947 Finger Plan?

o.o1: The city grows along five rail lines
o.o2: The harbour is extended with five islands
o.o3: The centre is split into five districts
o.o4: Five ring roads surround the city

kz-1xpbqo7.e: The palm is the old city, and the fingers are the S-train lines. Green wedges were meant to lie between the fingers.

kz-doveh6.p: True or false: The Eiffel Tower was originally meant to be torn down after 20 years.
kz-doveh6.e: The tower was built for the 1889 World's Fair. It survived because it proved useful as a radio mast.

kz-16catu3.p: True or false: The Leaning Tower of Pisa began to lean while it was being built.
kz-16catu3.e: The ground gave way once the third storey was reached. Construction stretched over almost 200 years.

kz-7yonyy.p: What originally said on the famous sign in the hills above Los Angeles?
kz-7yonyy.e: The sign was put up in 1923 as an advert for a residential development. The last four letters were removed in 1949.

kz-9vove4.p: Which 1927 film is considered the first feature film with sound?
kz-9vove4.e: Al Jolson's line that the audience had not heard anything yet heralded the end of silent films.

kz-1b775eu.p: Which actor has received the most Oscar nominations?
kz-1b775eu.e: Streep has been nominated 21 times and has won three.

kz-1u8k983.p: Which film studio has a roaring lion as its logo?
kz-1u8k983.e: Several different lions have lent their roar. The current one, Leo, has roared since 1957.

kz-1ooqwb6.p: Which director was known as “The Master of Suspense”?
kz-1ooqwb6.e: Hitchcock appears himself in a small cameo in almost all his films, but never won an Oscar for directing.

kz-1eiq9u.p: What is Quentin Tarantino's 1992 debut film called?
kz-1eiq9u.e: The film about a failed diamond heist never shows the heist itself.

kz-hrkrr6.p: Which film won Leonardo DiCaprio his first Oscar?
kz-hrkrr6.e: That happened in 2016, after four unsuccessful acting nominations.

kz-46b20t.p: Who plays Holly Golightly in Breakfast at Tiffany's?
kz-46b20t.e: The author Truman Capote would have preferred Marilyn Monroe in the role.

o.o1: An award for the year's worst film
o.o2: An award for the year's best stunt double
o.o3: An award for the best trailer
o.o4: An award for the year's best debut

kz-1o8q50s.e: The Golden Raspberry Awards are handed out the day before the Oscar ceremony. Sandra Bullock won both prizes the same weekend in 2010.

kz-1tlufyb.p: Which 1939 film is the highest-grossing ever when ticket prices are adjusted for inflation?
kz-1tlufyb.e: The film lasts almost four hours and won eight Oscars.

kz-6a2th3.p: Which 1937 film was Disney's first animated feature film?

o.o1: Snow White and the Seven Dwarfs

kz-6a2th3.e: The industry called the project “Disney's folly”. The film became the year's biggest hit.
